As `undefined` inherits defer time from the [series.animation.defer](#plotOptions.series.animation.defer).

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-className
title: className
description: A class name for styling by CSS.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-controlPointOptions
title: controlPointOptions
description:
Options for annotation's control points. Each control point
inherits options from controlPointOptions object.
Options from the controlPointOptions can be overwritten
by options in a specific control point.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-crop
title: crop
description:
Whether to hide the part of the annotation
that is outside the plot area.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-draggable
title: draggable
description:
Allow an annotation to be draggable by a user. Possible
values are `'x'`, `'xy'`, `'y'` and `''` (disabled).

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-events
title: events
description: Events available in annotations.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-events-add
title: add
description: Event callback when annotation is added to the chart.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-events-afterUpdate
title: afterUpdate
description:
Event callback when annotation is updated (e.g. drag and
dropped or resized by control points).

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-events-click
title: click
description: Fires when the annotation is clicked.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-events-drag
title: drag
description: Fires when the annotation is dragged.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-events-remove
title: remove
description: Event callback when annotation is removed from the chart.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-id
title: id
description:
Sets an ID for an annotation. Can be user later when
removing an annotation in [Chart#removeAnnotation(id)](/class-reference/Highcharts.Chart#removeAnnotation) method.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions
title: labelOptions
description:
Options for annotation's labels. Each label inherits options
from the labelOptions object. An option from the labelOptions
can be overwritten by config for a specific label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-accessibility
title: accessibility
description: Accessibility options for an annotation label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-accessibility-description
title: description
description:
Description of an annotation label for screen readers and other assistive
technology.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-align
title: align
description:
The alignment of the annotation's label. If right,
the right side of the label should be touching the point.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-allowOverlap
title: allowOverlap
description:
Whether to allow the annotation's labels to overlap.
To make the labels less sensitive for overlapping,
the can be set to 0.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description: The background color or gradient for the annotation's label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-borderColor
title: borderColor
description: The border color for the annotation's label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description: The border radius in pixels for the annotation's label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: The border width in pixels for the annotation's label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-className
title: className
description: A class name for styling by CSS.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-crop
title: crop
description:
Whether to hide the annotation's label
that is outside the plot area.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-distance
title: distance
description: The label's pixel distance from the point.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-format
title: format
description:
A
[format](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
string for the data label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the annotation's
label. Note that if a `format` or `text` are defined,
the format or text take precedence and the formatter is
ignored. `This` refers to a point object. The callback also receives
an argument `ctx` so that arrow-functions can access the same
context (the point in this case) as normal functions can using
`this`. Since v12.6.0, the callback receives `ctx`.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-includeInDataExport
title: includeInDataExport
description:
Whether all the labels for an annotation are visible in the exported
data table.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-overflow
title: overflow
description:
How to handle the annotation's label that flow outside
the plot area. The justify option aligns the label inside
the plot area.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-padding
title: padding
description:
When either the borderWidth or the backgroundColor is
set, this is the padding within the box.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-shadow
title: shadow
description:
The shadow of the box. The shadow can be an object
configuration containing `color`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`,
`opacity` and `width`.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the
label. Symbols are predefined functions on the Renderer
object.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-style
title: style
description: Styles for the annotation's label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-text
title: text
description: Alias for the format option.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to [use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the annotation's label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description: The vertical alignment of the annotation's label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-x
title: x
description:
The x position offset of the label relative to the point.
Note that if a `distance` is defined, the distance takes
precedence over `x` and `y` options.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labelOptions-y
title: y
description:
The y position offset of the label relative to the point.
Note that if a `distance` is defined, the distance takes
precedence over `x` and `y` options.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labels
title: labels
description:
An array of labels for the annotation. For options that apply
to multiple labels, they can be added to the
[labelOptions](annotations.labelOptions.html).

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labels-accessibility
title: accessibility
description: Accessibility options for an annotation label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labels-accessibility-description
title: description
description:
Description of an annotation label for screen readers and other assistive
technology.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labels-align
title: align
description:
The alignment of the annotation's label. If right,
the right side of the label should be touching the point.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labels-allowOverlap
title: allowOverlap
description:
Whether to allow the annotation's labels to overlap.
To make the labels less sensitive for overlapping,
the can be set to 0.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labels-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description: The background color or gradient for the annotation's label.

name: navigation-annotationsOptions-labels-borderColor

name: palette
title: palette
description:
The palette object specifies colors for the charts and how to apply them.

Each color scheme (`light` and `dark`) has three primary colors:
`backgroundColor`, `neutralColor`, and `highlightColor`. For the neutral and
highlight colors, a series of interpolated color variants are generated, and
accessed as CSS variables in the chart settings in their prefixed and
hyphenated form. For example,

* `var(--highcharts-neutral-color-80)` is a blend of the `neutralColor` and
  the `backgroundColor`, with a weight of 80% `neutralColor` and 20%
  `backgroundColor`. It is the default for the main title
  (`title.style.color`), axis labels and more.
* `var(--highcharts-highlight-color-80)` is a blend of the `highlightColor`
  and the `backgroundColor`, with a weight of 80% `highlightColor` and 20%
  `backgroundColor`. It is used for the zoom selection marker (with opacity),
  Stock Range Selector date input boxes and more.

The `colors` array is used for data series and points, and is not blended
with the `backgroundColor`. It is also accessible as CSS variables, and this
is the recommended way to hard-code colors to match series and data.
For example, `var(--highcharts-color-0)` is the first color in the `colors`
array, `var(--highcharts-color-1)` is the second color, and so on.

The palette only accepts plain color strings in the options. Gradients and
patterns are only supported in other color settings, such as `series.color`
or `point.color`, but they can use CSS variables from the palette.

name: palette-colorScheme
title: colorScheme
description:
Color scheme to use. When `light dark` is set, the chart will
automatically switch between light and dark mode based on the user's
system preferences, or whether the `.highcharts-light` or
`.highcharts-dark` class is applied to a parent of the container.

When `inherit` is set, the chart will inherit the color scheme from the
closest parent element with a defined color scheme, or default to `light`
if none is found.

name: palette-colors
title: colors
description:
Colors for data series and points. This setting is generic for both
light and dark mode, and can be overridden for each mode in
`light.colors` and `dark.colors`.

title: dark
description: Palette options for dark mode.

name: palette-dark-colors
title: colors
description:
Colors for data series and points. This array extends the colors
defined for the general `palette.colors` array, item by item. If an
item is `null` or `undefined`, the general color will be used.

name: palette-dark-negativeColor
title: negativeColor
description:
Negative color used in stock charts, such as for technical
indicators, annotations or hollow candlestick series.

name: palette-dark-positiveColor
title: positiveColor
description:
Positive color used in stock charts, such as for technical

description:

[css/highcharts-palette.css](https://code.highcharts.com/css/highcharts-palette.css).

description:

background is also used as base for interpolated neutral and

name: palette-light-colors
title: colors
description:
Colors for data series and points. This array extends the colors
defined for the general `palette.colors` array, item by item. If an

name: palette-light-highlightColor
title: highlightColor
description:
Highlight color to be used as base for interpolated colors. For
example, `var(--highcharts-highlight-color-60)` is a blend of the
`highlightColor` and the `backgroundColor`, with a weight of 60%
`highlightColor` and 40% `backgroundColor`.

Highlight colors are by default used for highlighted or active
elements, like the zoom selection marker, clickable Stock Range
Selector date input boxes, clickable drilldown labels and more.

name: palette-light-negativeColor
title: negativeColor
description:
Negative color used in stock charts, such as for technical
indicators, annotations or hollow candlestick series.

name: palette-light-neutralColor
title: neutralColor
description:
Neutral color to be used as base for interpolated colors. For
example, `var(--highcharts-neutral-color-60)` is a blend of the
`neutralColor` and the `backgroundColor`, with a weight of 60%
`neutralColor` and 40% `backgroundColor`.

Neutral colors are by default used for basic text, lines, borders,
basically most elements except the data itself, and highlighted
elements.

name: palette-light-positiveColor
title: positiveColor
description:
Positive color used in stock charts, such as for technical
indicators, annotations or hollow candlestick series.

name: plotOptions
title: plotOptions
description:
The plotOptions is a wrapper object for config objects for each series
type. The config objects for each series can also be overridden for
each series item as given in the series array.

Configuration options for the series are given in three levels. Options
for all series in a chart are given in the [plotOptions.series](#plotOptions.series) object. Then options for all series of a specific
type are given in the plotOptions of that type, for example
`plotOptions.line`. Next, options for one single series are given in
[the series array](#series).

name: plotOptions-contour
title: contour

name: plotOptions-contour-colorKey
title: colorKey
description:
This must be set to `'value'` to make the colorAxis track with the contour
plot.

name: plotOptions-contour-contourInterval
title: contourInterval
description:
The interval between contour lines. Determines the spacing of value
levels where lines are drawn on the plot. By default, the interval is
calculated using the value range.

name: plotOptions-contour-contourOffset
title: contourOffset
description:
The offset for contour line positioning. Shifts the contour levels so
lines and bands are drawn at `contourOffset + n * contourInterval`
instead of `n * contourInterval`.

Example: with `contourInterval: 10` and `contourOffset: 5`, levels are
at 5, 15, 25, etc. Use this to align levels with a reference value
without changing the data. Non-positive values are treated as 0.

name: plotOptions-contour-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: The color of the contour lines.

name: plotOptions-contour-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description:
This setting controls the visibility and size of contour lines. For now,
only '1' and '0' are valid options, effectively controlling the
visibility of the lines.

name: plotOptions-contour-marker-states-hover-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: Color of the marker outline. Defaults to `'black'`.

name: plotOptions-contour-marker-symbol
title: symbol
description:
A predefined shape or symbol for the marker. When undefined, the
symbol is pulled from options.symbols. Other possible values are
`'circle'`, `'square'`,`'diamond'`, `'triangle'`,
`'triangle-down'`, `'rect'`, `'ellipse'`, and `'cross'`.

Additionally, the URL to a graphic can be given on this form:
`'url(graphic.png)'`. Note that for the image to be applied to
exported charts, its URL needs to be accessible by the export
server.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols`. The callback is then
used by its method name, as shown in the demo.

name: plotOptions-contour-smoothColoring
title: smoothColoring
description:
Whether to use gradually transitioning color gradients between contour
levels. When disabled, each contour level is filled with a single flat
color.

name: plotOptions-flowmap
title: flowmap

name: plotOptions-flowmap-curveFactor
title: curveFactor
description:
The `curveFactor` option for all links. Value higher than 0 will
curve the link clockwise. A negative value will curve it counter
clockwise. If the value is 0 the link will be a straight line. By
default undefined curveFactor get an automatic curve.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
The fill color of all the links. If not set, the series color will be
used with the opacity set in
[fillOpacity](#plotOptions.flowmap.fillOpacity).

name: plotOptions-flowmap-fillOpacity
title: fillOpacity
description: The opacity of the color fill for all links.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Specify the `lineWidth` of the links if they are not specified.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-linkedTo
title: linkedTo
description:
The [id](#series.id) of another series to link to. Additionally, the
value can be ":previous" to link to the previous series. When two
series are linked, only the first one appears in the legend. Toggling
the visibility of this also toggles the linked series, which is
necessary for operations such as zoom or updates on the flowmap
series.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-markerEnd
title: markerEnd
description:
A `markerEnd` creates an arrow symbol indicating the direction of
flow at the destination. Specifying a `markerEnd` here will create
one for each link.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-markerEnd-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the `markerEnd`.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-markerEnd-height
title: height
description:
Height of the `markerEnd`. Can be a number in pixels or a
percentage based on the weight of the link.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-markerEnd-markerType
title: markerType
description:
Change the shape of the `markerEnd`.
Can be `arrow` or `mushroom`.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-markerEnd-width
title: width
description:
Width of the `markerEnd`. Can be a number in pixels or a
percentage based on the weight of the link.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-maxWidth
title: maxWidth
description:
Maximum width of a link expressed in pixels. The weight of a link is
mapped between `maxWidth` and `minWidth`.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-minWidth
title: minWidth
description:
Minimum width of a link expressed in pixels. The weight of a link is
mapped between `maxWidth` and `minWidth`.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-opacity
title: opacity
description:
The opacity of all the links. Affects the opacity for the entire
link, including stroke. See also
[fillOpacity](#plotOptions.flowmap.fillOpacity), that affects the
opacity of only the fill color.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-weight
title: weight
description:
The weight for all links with unspecified weights. The weight of a
link determines its thickness compared to other links.

name: plotOptions-flowmap-width
title: width
description:
If no weight has previously been specified, this will set the width
of all the links without being compared to and scaled according to
other weights.

name: plotOptions-geoheatmap
title: geoheatmap

name: plotOptions-geoheatmap-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The border width of each geoheatmap tile.

In styled mode, the border stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-point` class.

name: plotOptions-geoheatmap-color
title: color
description:
The main color of the series. In heat maps this color is rarely
used, as we mostly use the color to denote the value of each
point. Unless options are set in the [colorAxis](#colorAxis), the
default value is pulled from the [options.colors](#colors) array.

name: plotOptions-geoheatmap-colsize
title: colsize
description:
The column size - how many longitude units each column in the
geoheatmap should span.

name: plotOptions-geoheatmap-interpolation
title: interpolation
description:
Make the geoheatmap render its data points as an interpolated
image. It can be used to show a Temperature Map-like charts.

name: plotOptions-geoheatmap-interpolation-blur
title: blur
description:
Represents how much blur should be added to the interpolated
image. Works best in the range of 0-1, all higher values
would need a lot more performance of the machine to calculate
more detailed interpolation.

 * **Note:** Useful, if the data is spread into wide range of
 longitude and latitude values.

name: plotOptions-geoheatmap-interpolation-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the interpolation of the geoheatmap series.

name: plotOptions-geoheatmap-rowsize
title: rowsize
description:
The rowsize size - how many latitude units each row in the
geoheatmap should span.

name: plotOptions-heatmap
title: heatmap

name: plotOptions-heatmap-animation
title: animation
description: Animation is disabled by default on the heatmap series.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
The border radius for each heatmap item. The border's color and
width can be set in marker options.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: The border width for each heatmap item.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-colsize
title: colsize
description:
The column size - how many X axis units each column in the heatmap
should span.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-interpolation
title: interpolation
description: Make the heatmap render its data points as an interpolated image.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-height
title: height
description: Set the marker's fixed height on hover state.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-heightPlus
title: heightPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the height of the
selected point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-lineWidthPlus
title: lineWidthPlus
description: The additional line width for a hovered point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-width
title: width
description: Set the marker's fixed width on hover state.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-hover-widthPlus
title: widthPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the width of the
selected point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-select-height
title: height
description: Set the marker's fixed height on select state.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-select-heightPlus
title: heightPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the height of the
selected point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-select-width
title: width
description: Set the marker's fixed width on select state.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-states-select-widthPlus
title: widthPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the width of the
selected point.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-marker-symbol
title: symbol
description:
A predefined shape or symbol for the marker. When undefined, the
symbol is pulled from options.symbols. Other possible values are
`'circle'`, `'square'`,`'diamond'`, `'triangle'`,
`'triangle-down'`, `'rect'`, and `'ellipse'`.

Additionally, the URL to a graphic can be given on this form:
`'url(graphic.png)'`. Note that for the image to be applied to
exported charts, its URL needs to be accessible by the export
server.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols`. The callback is then
used by its method name, as shown in the demo.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-nullColor
title: nullColor
description:
The color applied to null points. In styled mode, a general CSS class
is applied instead.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-pointPadding
title: pointPadding
description: Padding between the points in the heatmap.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-rowsize
title: rowsize
description: The row size - how many Y axis units each heatmap row should span.

name: plotOptions-heatmap-states-hover-brightness
title: brightness
description:
How much to brighten the point on interaction.

In styled mode, the hover brightening is by default replaced
with a fill-opacity set in the `.highcharts-point:hover`
rule.

name: plotOptions-map
title: map

name: plotOptions-map-affectsMapView
title: affectsMapView
description:
Whether the MapView takes this series into account when computing the
default zoom and center of the map.

name: plotOptions-map-allAreas
title: allAreas
description:
Whether all areas of the map defined in `mapData` should be rendered.
If `true`, areas which don't correspond to a data point, are rendered
as `null` points. If `false`, those areas are skipped.

name: plotOptions-map-colorByPoint
title: colorByPoint
description:
When using automatic point colors pulled from the global
[colors](colors) or series-specific
[plotOptions.map.colors](series.colors) collections, this option
determines whether the chart should receive one color per series or
one color per point.

In styled mode, the `colors` or `series.colors` arrays are not
supported, and instead this option gives the points individual color
class names on the form `highcharts-color-{n}`.

name: plotOptions-map-colors
title: colors
description:
A series specific or series type specific color set to apply instead
of the global [colors](#colors) when [colorByPoint](#plotOptions.map.colorByPoint) is true.

name: plotOptions-map-nullColor
title: nullColor
description:
The color to apply to null points.

In styled mode, the null point fill is set in the
`.highcharts-null-point` class.

name: plotOptions-map-nullInteraction
title: nullInteraction
description:
Whether to allow pointer interaction like tooltips and mouse events
on null points.

name: plotOptions-map-shadow
title: shadow
description:
Whether to apply a drop shadow to the map shapes. The shadow can be an
object configuration containing `color`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `opacity`
and `width`.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble
title: mapbubble

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-color
title: color
description:
The main color of the series. This color affects both the fill
and the stroke of the bubble. For enhanced control, use `marker`
options.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-displayNegative
title: displayNegative
description:
Whether to display negative sized bubbles. The threshold is
given by the [zThreshold](#plotOptions.mapbubble.zThreshold)
option, and negative bubbles can be visualized by setting
[negativeColor](#plotOptions.bubble.negativeColor).

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
Color of the line connecting bubbles. The default value is the same
as series' color.

In styled mode, the color can be defined by the
[colorIndex](#plotOptions.series.colorIndex) option. Also, the series
color can be set with the `.highcharts-series`,
`.highcharts-color-{n}`, `.highcharts-{type}-series` or
`.highcharts-series-{n}` class, or individual classes given by the
`className` option.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Pixel width of the line connecting bubbles.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-maxSize
title: maxSize
description:
Maximum bubble size. Bubbles will automatically size between the
`minSize` and `maxSize` to reflect the `z` value of each bubble.
Can be either pixels (when no unit is given), or a percentage of
the smallest one of the plot width and height.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-minSize
title: minSize
description:
Minimum bubble size. Bubbles will automatically size between the
`minSize` and `maxSize` to reflect the `z` value of each bubble.
Can be either pixels (when no unit is given), or a percentage of
the smallest one of the plot width and height.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-negativeColor
title: negativeColor
description:
When a point's Z value is below the
[zThreshold](#plotOptions.mapbubble.zThreshold) setting, this
color is used.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-sizeBy
title: sizeBy
description:
Whether the bubble's value should be represented by the area or
the width of the bubble. The default, `area`, corresponds best to
the human perception of the size of each bubble.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-sizeByAbsoluteValue
title: sizeByAbsoluteValue
description:
When this is true, the absolute value of z determines the size
of the bubble. This means that with the default `zThreshold` of
0, a bubble of value -1 will have the same size as a bubble of
value 1, while a bubble of value 0 will have a smaller size
according to `minSize`.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-zMax
title: zMax
description:
The maximum for the Z value range. Defaults to the highest Z value in
the data.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-zMin
title: zMin
description:
The minimum for the Z value range. Defaults to the lowest Z value
in the data.

name: plotOptions-mapbubble-zThreshold
title: zThreshold
description:
When [displayNegative](#plotOptions.mapbubble.displayNegative)
is `false`, bubbles with lower Z values are skipped. When
`displayNegative` is `true` and a
[negativeColor](#plotOptions.mapbubble.negativeColor) is given,
points with lower Z is colored.

name: plotOptions-mapline
title: mapline

name: plotOptions-mapline-fillColor
title: fillColor
description: Fill color for the map line shapes

name: plotOptions-mapline-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Pixel width of the mapline line.

name: plotOptions-mapline-states-hover-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Pixel width of the mapline line.

name: plotOptions-mappoint
title: mappoint

name: plotOptions-pie
title: pie

name: plotOptions-pie-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The color of the border surrounding each slice. When `null`, the
border takes the same color as the slice fill. This can be used
together with a `borderWidth` to fill drawing gaps created by
antialiasing artifacts in border-less pies.

In styled mode, the border stroke is given in the `.highcharts-point`
class.

name: plotOptions-pie-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
The corner radius of the border surrounding each slice. A number
signifies pixels. A percentage string, like for example `50%`, signifies
a size relative to the radius and the inner radius.

name: plotOptions-pie-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The width of the border surrounding each slice.

When setting the border width to 0, there may be small gaps between
the slices due to SVG antialiasing artifacts. To work around this,
keep the border width at 0.5 or 1, but set the `borderColor` to
`null` instead.

In styled mode, the border stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-point` class.

name: plotOptions-pie-center
title: center
description:
The center of the pie chart relative to the plot area. Can be
percentages or pixel values. The default behavior (as of 3.0) is to
center the pie so that all slices and data labels are within the plot
area. As a consequence, the pie may actually jump around in a chart
with dynamic values, as the data labels move. In that case, the
center should be explicitly set, for example to `["50%", "50%"]`.

name: plotOptions-pie-color
title: color
description:
The color of the pie series. A pie series is represented as an empty
circle if the total sum of its values is 0. Use this property to
define the color of its border.

In styled mode, the color can be defined by the
[colorIndex](#plotOptions.series.colorIndex) option. Also, the series
color can be set with the `.highcharts-series`,
`.highcharts-color-{n}`, `.highcharts-{type}-series` or
`.highcharts-series-{n}` class, or individual classes given by the
`className` option.

name: plotOptions-pie-colors
title: colors
description:
A series specific or series type specific color set to use instead
of the global [colors](#colors).

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-alignTo
title: alignTo
description:
Alignment method for data labels. Possible values are:

- `plotEdges`: Each label touches the nearest vertical edge of
  the plot area.

- `connectors`: Connectors have the same x position and the
  widest label of each half (left & right) touches the nearest
  vertical edge of the plot area.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-connectorColor
title: connectorColor
description:
The color of the line connecting the data label to the pie slice.
The default color is the same as the point's color.

In styled mode, the connector stroke is given in the
`.highcharts-data-label-connector` class.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-connectorPadding
title: connectorPadding
description:
The distance from the data label to the connector. Note that
data labels also have a default `padding`, so in order for the
connector to touch the text, the `padding` must also be 0.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-connectorShape
title: connectorShape
description:
Specifies the method that is used to generate the connector path.
Highcharts provides 3 built-in connector shapes: `'crookedLine'`
(default since v11), `'fixedOffset'` and `'straight'`.

Users can provide their own method by passing a function instead of a
string. Three arguments are passed to the callback:

- An object that holds the information about the coordinates of the
  label (`x` & `y` properties) and how the label is located in
  relation to the pie (`alignment` property). `alignment` can by one
  of the following: `'left'` (pie on the left side of the data
  label), `'right'` (pie on the right side of the data label) or
  `'center'` (data label overlaps the pie).

- An object that holds the information about the position of the
  connector. Its `touchingSliceAt` property tells the position of
  the place where the connector touches the slice.

- Data label options

The function has to return an SVG path definition in array form (see
the example).

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-connectorWidth
title: connectorWidth
description:
The width of the line connecting the data label to the pie slice.

In styled mode, the connector stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-data-label-connector` class.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-crookDistance
title: crookDistance
description:
Works only if `connectorShape` is `'crookedLine'`. It defines how
far from the vertical plot edge the connector path should be
crooked. With the default, `undefined`, the crook is placed so that
the horizontal line from the label intersects with the radial line
extending through the center of the pie slice.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-distance
title: distance
description:
The distance of the data label from the pie's edge. Negative
numbers put the data label on top of the pie slices. Can also be
defined as a percentage of pie's radius. Connectors are only
shown for data labels outside the pie.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-format
title: format
description:
A
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for the data label. Available variables are the same as for
`formatter`.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the data label. Note that
if a `format` is defined, the format takes precedence and the
formatter is ignored.

name: plotOptions-pie-dataLabels-softConnector
title: softConnector
description:
Whether to render the connector as a soft arc or a line with a sharp
break. Works only if `connectorShape` equals to `fixedOffset`.

name: plotOptions-pie-endAngle
title: endAngle
description:
The end angle of the pie in degrees where 0 is top and 90 is right.
Defaults to `startAngle` plus 360.

name: plotOptions-pie-events-checkboxClick
title: checkboxClick
description:
Fires when the checkbox next to the point name in the legend is
clicked. One parameter, event, is passed to the function. The state
of the checkbox is found by event.checked. The checked item is found
by event.item. Return false to prevent the default action which is to
toggle the select state of the series.

name: plotOptions-pie-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
If the total sum of the pie's values is 0, the series is represented
as an empty circle . The `fillColor` option defines the color of that
circle. Use [pie.borderWidth](#plotOptions.pie.borderWidth) to set
the border thickness.

name: plotOptions-pie-ignoreHiddenPoint
title: ignoreHiddenPoint
description:
Equivalent to [chart.ignoreHiddenSeries](#chart.ignoreHiddenSeries),
this option tells whether the series shall be redrawn as if the
hidden point were `null`.

The default value changed from `false` to `true` with Highcharts
3.0.

name: plotOptions-pie-innerSize
title: innerSize
description:
The size of the inner diameter for the pie. A size greater than 0
renders a donut chart. Can be a percentage or pixel value.
Percentages are relative to the pie size. Pixel values are given as
integers. Setting overridden by thickness.


Note: in Highcharts < 4.1.2, the percentage was relative to the plot
area, not the pie size.

name: plotOptions-pie-minSize
title: minSize

name: plotOptions-pie-showInLegend
title: showInLegend
description:
Whether to display this particular series or series type in the
legend. Since 2.1, pies are not shown in the legend by default.

name: plotOptions-pie-size
title: size
description:
The diameter of the pie relative to the plot area. Can be a
percentage or pixel value. Pixel values are given as integers. The
default behavior (as of 3.0) is to scale to the plot area and give
room for data labels within the plot area.
[slicedOffset](#plotOptions.pie.slicedOffset) is also included in the
default size calculation. As a consequence, the size of the pie may
vary when points are updated and data labels more around. In that
case it is best to set a fixed value, for example `"75%"`.

name: plotOptions-pie-slicedOffset
title: slicedOffset
description:
If a point is sliced, moved out from the center, how many pixels
should it be moved?.

name: plotOptions-pie-startAngle
title: startAngle
description:
The start angle of the pie slices in degrees where 0 is top and 90
right.

name: plotOptions-pie-states-hover-brightness
title: brightness
description:
How much to brighten the point on interaction.

In styled mode, the hover brightness is by default replaced
by a fill-opacity given in the `.highcharts-point-hover`
class.

name: plotOptions-pie-stickyTracking
title: stickyTracking
description:
Sticky tracking of mouse events. When true, the `mouseOut` event
on a series isn't triggered until the mouse moves over another
series, or out of the plot area. When false, the `mouseOut` event on
a series is triggered when the mouse leaves the area around the
series'  graph or markers. This also implies the tooltip. When
`stickyTracking` is false and `tooltip.shared` is false, the tooltip
will be hidden when moving the mouse between series.

name: plotOptions-scatter
title: scatter

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster
title: cluster
description:
Options for marker clusters, the concept of sampling the data
values into larger blocks in order to ease readability and
increase performance of the JavaScript charts.

Note: marker clusters module is not working with `boost`
and `draggable-points` modules.

The marker clusters feature requires the marker-clusters.js
file to be loaded, found in the modules directory of the download
package, or online at [code.highcharts.com/modules/marker-clusters.js](code.highcharts.com/modules/marker-clusters.js).

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-allowOverlap
title: allowOverlap
description:
When set to `false` prevent cluster overlapping - this option
works only when `layoutAlgorithm.type = "grid"`.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-animation
title: animation
description: Options for the cluster marker animation.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description: Options for the cluster data labels.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-drillToCluster
title: drillToCluster
description: Zoom the plot area to the cluster points range when a cluster is clicked.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether to enable the marker-clusters module.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-events-drillToCluster
title: drillToCluster
description:
Fires when the cluster point is clicked and `drillToCluster` is enabled.
One parameter, `event`, is passed to the function. The default action
is to zoom to the cluster points range. This can be prevented
by calling `event.preventDefault()`.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm
title: layoutAlgorithm
description:
Options for layout algorithm. Inside there
are options to change the type of the algorithm, gridSize,
distance or iterations.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-distance
title: distance
description:
When `type` is set to `kmeans`,
`distance` is a maximum distance between point and cluster center
so that this point will be inside the cluster. The distance
is either a number defining pixels or a percentage
defining a percentage of the plot area width.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-gridSize
title: gridSize
description:
When `type` is set to the `grid`,
`gridSize` is a size of a grid square element either as a number
defining pixels, or a percentage defining a percentage
of the plot area width.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-iterations
title: iterations
description:
When `type` is set to `kmeans`,
`iterations` are the number of iterations that this algorithm will be
repeated to find clusters positions.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-kmeansThreshold
title: kmeansThreshold
description:
When `type` is set to `undefined` and there are more visible points
than the kmeansThreshold the `grid` algorithm is used to find
clusters, otherwise `kmeans`. It ensures good performance on
large datasets and better clusters arrangement after the zoom.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-layoutAlgorithm-type
title: type
description:
Type of the algorithm used to combine points into a cluster. There are three available algorithms: 1) `grid` - grid-based clustering technique. Points are assigned to squares of set size depending on their position on the plot area. Points inside the grid square are combined into a cluster. The grid size can be controlled by `gridSize` property (grid size changes at certain zoom levels). 2) `kmeans` - based on K-Means clustering technique. In the first step, points are divided using the grid method (distance property is a grid size) to find the initial amount of clusters. Next, each point is classified by computing the distance between each cluster center and that point. When the closest cluster distance is lower than distance property set by a user the point is added to this cluster otherwise is classified as `noise`. The algorithm is repeated until each cluster center not change its previous position more than one pixel. This technique is more accurate but also more time consuming than the `grid` algorithm, especially for big datasets. 3) `optimizedKmeans` - based on K-Means clustering technique. This algorithm uses k-means algorithm only on the chart initialization or when chart extremes have greater range than on initialization. When a chart is redrawn the algorithm checks only clustered points distance from the cluster center and rebuild it when the point is spaced enough to be outside the cluster. It provides performance improvement and more stable clusters position yet can be used rather on small and sparse datasets. By default, the algorithm depends on visible quantity of points and `kmeansThreshold`. When there are more visible points than the `kmeansThreshold` the `grid` algorithm is used, otherwise `kmeans`. The custom clustering algorithm can be added by assigning a callback function as the type property. This function takes an array of `processedXData`, `processedYData`, `processedXData` indexes and `layoutAlgorithm` options as arguments and should return an object with grouped data. The algorithm should return an object like that: 
{
 clusterId1: [{
     x: 573,
     y: 285,
     index: 1 // point index in the data array
 }, {
     x: 521,
     y: 197,
     index: 2
 }],
 clusterId2: [{
     ...
 }]
 ...
}
`clusterId` (example above - unique id of a cluster or noise) is an array of points belonging to a cluster. If the array has only one point or fewer points than set in `cluster.minimumClusterSize` it won't be combined into a cluster.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-marker
title: marker
description: Options for the cluster marker.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-minimumClusterSize
title: minimumClusterSize
description:
The minimum amount of points to be combined into a cluster.
This value has to be greater or equal to 2.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-states-hover-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
The fill color of the cluster marker in hover state. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's fillColor for normal
state is used.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones
title: zones
description:
An array defining zones within marker clusters.

In styled mode, the color zones are styled with the
`.highcharts-cluster-zone-{n}` class, or custom
classed from the `className`
option.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones-className
title: className
description: Styled mode only. A custom class name for the zone.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones-from
title: from
description: The value where the zone starts.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones-marker
title: marker
description: Settings for the cluster marker belonging to the zone.

name: plotOptions-scatter-cluster-zones-to
title: to
description: The value where the zone ends.

name: plotOptions-scatter-stickyTracking
title: stickyTracking
description:
Sticky tracking of mouse events. When true, the `mouseOut` event
on a series isn't triggered until the mouse moves over another
series, or out of the plot area. When false, the `mouseOut` event on
a series is triggered when the mouse leaves the area around the
series' graph or markers. This also implies the tooltip. When
`stickyTracking` is false and `tooltip.shared` is false, the tooltip
will be hidden when moving the mouse between series.

name: plotOptions-scatter-tooltip
title: tooltip
description:
A configuration object for the tooltip rendering of each single
series. Properties are inherited from [tooltip](#tooltip).
Overridable properties are `headerFormat`, `pointFormat`,
`yDecimals`, `xDateFormat`, `yPrefix` and `ySuffix`. Unlike other
series, in a scatter plot the series.name by default shows in the
headerFormat and point.x and point.y in the pointFormat.

name: plotOptions-series
title: series

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility
title: accessibility
description: Accessibility options for a series.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-description
title: description
description: Provide a description of the series, announced to screen readers.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-descriptionFormat
title: descriptionFormat
description:
Format to use for describing the data series group to assistive
technology - including screen readers.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable/disable accessibility functionality for a specific series.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-exposeAsGroupOnly
title: exposeAsGroupOnly
description: Expose only the series element to screen readers, not its points.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-keyboardNavigation
title: keyboardNavigation
description: Keyboard navigation for a series

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-keyboardNavigation-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable/disable keyboard navigation support for a specific series.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point
title: point
description: Point accessibility options for a series.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-dateFormat
title: dateFormat
description:
Date format to use for points on datetime axes when describing
them to screen reader users.

Defaults to the same format as in tooltip.

For an overview of the replacement codes, see
[dateFormat](/class-reference/Highcharts.Time#dateFormat).

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-dateFormatter
title: dateFormatter
description:
Formatter function to determine the date/time format used with
points on datetime axes when describing them to screen reader
users. Receives one argument, `point`, referring to the point
to describe. Should return a date format string compatible with
[dateFormat](/class-reference/Highcharts.Time#dateFormat).

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-describeNull
title: describeNull
description:
Whether or not to describe points with the value `null` to
assistive technology, such as screen readers.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-descriptionFormat
title: descriptionFormat
description:
A [format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
to use instead of the default for point descriptions.

The context of the format string is the point instance.

As opposed to [accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat](#accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat),
this option replaces the whole description.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-descriptionFormatter
title: descriptionFormatter
description:
Formatter function to use instead of the default for point
descriptions. Same as `accessibility.point.descriptionFormatter`, but
applies to a series instead of the whole chart.

Note: Prefer using [accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat](#plotOptions.series.accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat)
instead if possible, as default functionality such as describing
annotations will be preserved.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-valueDecimals
title: valueDecimals
description:
Decimals to use for the values in the point descriptions. Uses
[tooltip.valueDecimals](#tooltip.valueDecimals) if not defined.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-valueDescriptionFormat
title: valueDescriptionFormat
description:
Format to use for describing the values of data points
to assistive technology - including screen readers.
The point context is available as `{point}`.

Other available context variables include `{index}`, `{value}`, and `{xDescription}`.

Additionally, the series name, annotation info, and
description added in `point.accessibility.description`
is added by default if relevant. To override this, use the
[accessibility.point.descriptionFormatter](#accessibility.point.descriptionFormatter)
option.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-valuePrefix
title: valuePrefix
description:
Prefix to add to the values in the point descriptions. Uses
[tooltip.valuePrefix](#tooltip.valuePrefix) if not defined.

name: plotOptions-series-accessibility-point-valueSuffix
title: valueSuffix
description:
Suffix to add to the values in the point descriptions. Uses
[tooltip.valueSuffix](#tooltip.valueSuffix) if not defined.

name: plotOptions-series-allowPointSelect
title: allowPointSelect
description:
Allow this series' points to be selected by clicking on the graphic
(columns, point markers, pie slices, map areas etc).

The selected points can be handled by point select and unselect
events, or collectively by the [getSelectedPoints](/class-reference/Highcharts.Chart#getSelectedPoints) function.

And alternative way of selecting points is through dragging.

name: plotOptions-series-animation
title: animation
description:
Enable or disable the initial animation when a series is displayed.
The animation can also be set as a configuration object. Please
note that this option only applies to the initial animation of the
series itself. For other animations, see [chart.animation](#chart.animation) and the animation parameter under the API methods.
The following properties are supported:

- `defer`: The animation delay time in milliseconds.

- `duration`: The duration of the animation in milliseconds. (Defaults to
  `1000`)

- `easing`: Can be a string reference to an easing function set on
  the `Math` object or a function. See the _Custom easing function_
  demo below. (Defaults to `easeInOutSine`)

Due to poor performance, animation is disabled in old IE browsers
for several chart types.

name: plotOptions-series-animationLimit
title: animationLimit
description:
For some series, there is a limit that shuts down animation
by default when the total number of points in the chart is too high.
For example, for a column chart and its derivatives, animation does
not run if there is more than 250 points totally. To disable this
cap, set `animationLimit` to `Infinity`. This option works if animation
is fired on individual points, not on a group of points like e.g. during
the initial animation.

name: plotOptions-series-boostBlending
title: boostBlending
description: Sets the color blending in the boost module.

name: plotOptions-series-boostThreshold
title: boostThreshold
description:
Set the point threshold for when a series should enter boost mode.

Setting it to e.g. 2000 will cause the series to enter boost mode when there
are 2000 or more points in the series.

To disable boosting on the series, set the `boostThreshold` to 0. Setting it
to 1 will force boosting.

Note that the [cropThreshold](plotOptions.series.cropThreshold) also affects
this setting. When zooming in on a series that has fewer points than the
`cropThreshold`, all points are rendered although outside the visible plot
area, and the `boostThreshold` won't take effect.

name: plotOptions-series-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The border color of the map areas.

In styled mode, the border stroke is given in the `.highcharts-point`
class.

name: plotOptions-series-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The border width of each map area.

In styled mode, the border stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-point` class.

name: plotOptions-series-className
title: className
description:
An additional class name to apply to the series' graphical elements.
This option does not replace default class names of the graphical
element. Changes to the series' color will also be reflected in a
chart's legend and tooltip.

name: plotOptions-series-clip
title: clip
description:
Disable this option to allow series rendering in the whole plotting
area.

**Note:** Clipping should be always enabled when
[chart.zoomType](#chart.zoomType) is set

name: plotOptions-series-color
title: color
description:
The main color of the series. In line type series it applies to the
line and the point markers unless otherwise specified. In bar type
series it applies to the bars unless a color is specified per point.
The default value is pulled from the `options.colors` array.

In styled mode, the color can be defined by the
[colorIndex](#plotOptions.series.colorIndex) option. Also, the series
color can be set with the `.highcharts-series`,
`.highcharts-color-{n}`, `.highcharts-{type}-series` or
`.highcharts-series-{n}` class, or individual classes given by the
`className` option.

name: plotOptions-series-colorAxis
title: colorAxis
description:
When using dual or multiple color axes, this number defines which
colorAxis the particular series is connected to. It refers to
either the
{@link #colorAxis.id|axis id}
or the index of the axis in the colorAxis array, with 0 being the
first. Set this option to false to prevent a series from connecting
to the default color axis.

Since v7.2.0 the option can also be an axis id or an axis index
instead of a boolean flag.

name: plotOptions-series-colorIndex
title: colorIndex
description:
Styled mode only. A specific color index to use for the series, so its
graphic representations are given the class name `highcharts-color-{n}`.

Since v11, CSS variables on the form `--highcharts-color-{n}` make
changing the color scheme very convenient.

name: plotOptions-series-colorKey
title: colorKey
description:
Determines what data value should be used to calculate point color
if `colorAxis` is used. Requires to set `min` and `max` if some
custom point property is used or if approximation for data grouping
is set to `'sum'`.

name: plotOptions-series-cursor
title: cursor
description:
You can set the cursor to "pointer" if you have click events attached
to the series, to signal to the user that the points and lines can
be clicked.

In styled mode, the series cursor can be set with the same classes
as listed under [series.color](#plotOptions.series.color).

name: plotOptions-series-custom
title: custom
description:
A reserved subspace to store options and values for customized
functionality. Here you can add additional data for your own event
callbacks and formatter callbacks.

name: plotOptions-series-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description:
Name of the dash style to use for the graph, or for some series types
the outline of each shape.

In styled mode, the
[stroke dash-array](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/css/series-dashstyle/)
can be set with the same classes as listed under
[series.color](#plotOptions.series.color).

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Options for the series data labels, appearing next to each data point.

Since v6.2.0, multiple data labels can be applied to each single
point by defining them as an array of configs.

In styled mode, the data labels can be styled with the
`.highcharts-data-label-box` and `.highcharts-data-label` class names
([see example](https://www.highcharts.com/samples/highcharts/css/series-datalabels)).

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-align
title: align
description:
The alignment of the data label compared to the point. If `right`,
the right side of the label should be touching the point. For points
with an extent, like columns, the alignments also dictates how to
align it inside the box, as given with the
[inside](#plotOptions.column.dataLabels.inside) option. Can be one of
`left`, `center` or `right`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-alignTo
title: alignTo
description:
Alignment method for data labels. If set to `plotEdges`, the labels
are aligned within the plot area in the direction of the y-axis. So
in a regular column chart, the labels are aligned vertically
according to the `verticalAlign` setting. In a bar chart, which is
inverted, the labels are aligned horizontally according to the
`align` setting. Applies to cartesian series only.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-allowOverlap
title: allowOverlap
description:
Whether to allow data labels to overlap. To make the labels less
sensitive for overlapping, the
[dataLabels.padding](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.padding)
can be set to 0.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-animation
title: animation
description:
Enable or disable the initial animation when a series is displayed
for the `dataLabels`. The animation can also be set as a
configuration object. Please note that this option only applies to
the initial animation.

For other animations, see [chart.animation](#chart.animation) and the
animation parameter under the API methods. The following properties
are supported:

- `defer`: The animation delay time in milliseconds.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-animation-defer
title: defer
description:
The animation delay time in milliseconds. Set to `0` to render the
data labels immediately. As `undefined` inherits defer time from the
[series.animation.defer](#plotOptions.series.animation.defer).

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
The background color or gradient for the data label. In addition to
regular colors, there are two special setting for this option:
- `auto` will set the background color the point's color.
- `contrast` will set it to a contrast against the text color, with
  an opacity allowing to see the underlying content. The contrast is
  great enough to ensure readability for the text according to
  accessibility standards.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The border color for the data label. Setting it to `auto` will use
the point's color. Defaults to `undefined`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description: The border radius in pixels for the data label.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: The border width in pixels for the data label.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-className
title: className
description:
A class name for the data label. Particularly in styled mode,
this can be used to give each series' or point's data label
unique styling. In addition to this option, a default color class
name is added so that we can give the labels a contrast text
shadow.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-crop
title: crop
description:
Whether to hide data labels that are outside the plot area. By
default, the data label is moved inside the plot area according
to the
[overflow](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.overflow)
option.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the data labels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-filter
title: filter
description:
A declarative filter to control of which data labels to display.
The declarative filter is designed for use when callback
functions are not available, like when the chart options require
a pure JSON structure or for use with graphical editors. For
programmatic control, use the `formatter` instead, and return
`undefined` to disable a single data label.

```js
filter: {
    property: 'percentage',
    operator: '>',
    value: 4
}
```

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-filter-operator
title: operator
description:
The operator to compare by. Can be one of `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`,
`==`, `===`, `!=` and `!==`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-filter-property
title: property
description:
The point property to filter by. Point options are passed
directly to properties, additionally there are `y` value,
`percentage` and others listed under {@link Highcharts.Point}
members.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-filter-value
title: value
description: The value to compare against.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-format
title: format
description:
A
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for the data label. Available variables are the same as for
`formatter`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the data label. Note that if a
`format` is defined, the format takes precedence and the formatter is
ignored.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-inside
title: inside
description:
For points with an extent, like columns or map areas, whether to
align the data label inside the box or to the actual value point.
Defaults to `false` in most cases, `true` in stacked columns.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-labelrank
title: labelrank
description:
The rank for this point's data label in case of collision. If two
data labels are about to overlap, only the one with the highest
`labelrank` will be drawn.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-nullFormat
title: nullFormat
description:
Format for points with the value of null. Works analogously to
[format](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.format). `nullFormat` can
be applied only to series which support displaying null points.
`heatmap` and `tilemap` supports `nullFormat` by default while the
following series requires [#series.nullInteraction] set to `true`:
`line`, `spline`, `area`, `area-spline`, `column`, `bar`, and
`timeline`. Does not work with series that don't display null
points, like `pie`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-nullFormatter
title: nullFormatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function that defines formatting for points
with the value of null. Works analogously to
[formatter](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.formatter).
`nullFormatter` can be applied only to series which support
displaying null points. `heatmap` and `tilemap` supports
`nullFormatter` by default while the following series requires
(series.nullInteraction)[#series.nullInteraction]
set to `true`: `line`, `spline`, `area`, `area-spline`, `column`,
`bar`, and `timeline`. Does not work with series that don't display
null points, like `pie`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-overflow
title: overflow
description:
How to handle data labels that flow outside the plot area. The
default is `"justify"`, which aligns them inside the plot area.
For columns and bars, this means it will be moved inside the bar.
To display data labels outside the plot area, set `crop` to
`false` and `overflow` to `"allow"`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-padding
title: padding
description:
When either the `borderWidth` or the `backgroundColor` is set,
this is the padding within the box.

An array of numbers sets padding for the respective sides. An array
of two numbers repeats the values for the horizontal and vertical
sides.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-position
title: position
description:
Aligns data labels relative to points. If `center` alignment is
not possible, it defaults to `right`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-rotation
title: rotation
description:
Text rotation in degrees. Note that due to a more complex
structure, backgrounds, borders and padding will be lost on a
rotated data label.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-shadow
title: shadow
description:
The shadow of the box. Works best with `borderWidth` or
`backgroundColor`. Since 2.3 the shadow can be an object
configuration containing `color`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `opacity`
and `width`.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the label.
Symbols are predefined functions on the Renderer object.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-style
title: style
description:
Styles for the label. The default `color` setting is
`"contrast"`, which is a pseudo color that Highcharts picks up
and applies the maximum contrast to the underlying point item,
for example the bar in a bar chart.

The `textOutline` is a pseudo property that applies an outline of
the given width with the given color, which by default is the
maximum contrast to the text. So a bright text color will result
in a black text outline for maximum readability on a mixed
background. In some cases, especially with grayscale text, the
text outline doesn't work well, in which cases it can be disabled
by setting it to `"none"`. When `useHTML` is true, the
`textOutline` will not be picked up. In this, case, the same
effect can be achieved through the `text-shadow` CSS property. As a
complementary or alternative to the `textOutline`, a
`dataLabels.backgroundColor` can be used. It provides a more calm
impression and ensures readable text label, at the cost of a risk of
overshadowing the underlying chart elements.

For some series types, where each point has an extent, like for
example tree maps, the data label may overflow the point. There
are two strategies for handling overflow. By default, the text
will wrap to multiple lines. The other strategy is to set
`style.textOverflow` to `ellipsis`, which will keep the text on
one line plus it will break inside long words.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-textPath
title: textPath
description:
Options for a label text which should follow marker's shape.
Border and background are disabled for a label that follows a
path.

**Note:** Only SVG-based renderer supports this option. Setting
`useHTML` to true will disable this option.

Text path support is not bundled into `highcharts.js`, and requires the
`modules/textpath.js` file. However, it is included in the script files of
those series types that use it by default.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-textPath-attributes
title: attributes
description: Presentation attributes for the text path.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-textPath-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable or disable `textPath` option for link's or marker's data
labels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to
[use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the labels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
The vertical alignment of a data label. Can be one of `top`,
`middle` or `bottom`. The default value depends on the data, for
instance in a column chart, the label is above positive values
and below negative values.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-x
title: x
description:
The x position offset of the label relative to the point in
pixels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-y
title: y
description:
The y position offset of the label relative to the point in
pixels.

name: plotOptions-series-dataLabels-zIndex
title: zIndex
description:
The z index of the data labels group. Does not apply below series
level options.

Use a `zIndex` of 6 to display it above the series,
or use a `zIndex` of 2 to display it behind the series.

name: plotOptions-series-dataMapping
title: dataMapping

name: plotOptions-series-dataTable
title: dataTable
description:
Options for a specific series-level data table or an array of data
tables. The `dataTable` option can be either a configuration object or an
instance of the `DataTable` class. If a `DataTable` instance is passed,
it will be used directly. If a configuration object or an array is
passed, a new `DataTable` instance will be created based on the provided
configuration.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop
title: dragDrop
description:
The draggable-points module allows points to be moved around or modified in
the chart. In addition to the options mentioned under the `dragDrop` API
structure, the module fires three events,
[point.dragStart](plotOptions.series.point.events.dragStart),
[point.drag](plotOptions.series.point.events.drag) and
[point.drop](plotOptions.series.point.events.drop).

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle
title: dragHandle
description: Options for the drag handles available in column series.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-className
title: className
description: The class name of the drag handles. Defaults to `highcharts-drag-handle`.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-color
title: color
description: The fill color of the drag handles.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: The line color of the drag handles.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The line width for the drag handles.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragHandle-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The z index for the drag handles.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragMaxX
title: dragMaxX
description: Set the maximum X value the points can be moved to.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragMaxY
title: dragMaxY
description: Set the maximum Y value the points can be moved to.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragMinX
title: dragMinX
description: Set the minimum X value the points can be moved to.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragMinY
title: dragMinY
description: Set the minimum Y value the points can be moved to.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragPrecisionX
title: dragPrecisionX
description:
The X precision value to drag to for this series. Set to 0 to disable. By
default this is disabled, except for category axes, where the default is
`1`.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragPrecisionY
title: dragPrecisionY
description:
The Y precision value to drag to for this series. Set to 0 to disable. By
default this is disabled, except for category axes, where the default is
`1`.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-dragSensitivity
title: dragSensitivity
description:
The amount of pixels to drag the pointer before it counts as a drag
operation. This prevents drag/drop to fire when just clicking or
selecting points.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-draggableX
title: draggableX
description: Enable dragging in the X dimension.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-draggableY
title: draggableY
description:
Enable dragging in the Y dimension. Note that this is not supported for
TreeGrid axes (the default axis type in Gantt charts).

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-groupBy
title: groupBy
description:
Group the points by a property. Points with the same property value will
be grouped together when moving.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox
title: guideBox
description:
Style options for the guide box. The guide box has one state by default,
the `default` state.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default
title: default
description: Style options for the guide box default state.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-className
title: className
description:
CSS class name of the guide box in this state. Defaults to
`highcharts-drag-box-default`.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-color
title: color
description: Guide box fill color.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-cursor
title: cursor
description: Guide box cursor.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: Color of the border around the guide box.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Width of the line around the guide box.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: Guide box zIndex.

name: plotOptions-series-dragDrop-liveRedraw
title: liveRedraw
description:
Update points as they are dragged. If false, a guide box is drawn to
illustrate the new point size.

name: plotOptions-series-enableMouseTracking
title: enableMouseTracking
description:
Enable or disable the mouse tracking for a specific series. This
includes point tooltips and click events on graphs and points. For
large datasets it improves performance.

name: plotOptions-series-events
title: events
description:
General event handlers for the series items. These event hooks can
also be attached to the series at run time using the
`Highcharts.addEvent` function.

name: plotOptions-series-events-checkboxClick
title: checkboxClick
description:
Fires when the checkbox next to the series' name in the legend is
clicked. One parameter, `event`, is passed to the function. The state
of the checkbox is found by `event.checked`. The checked item is
found by `event.item`. Return `false` to prevent the default action
which is to toggle the select state of the series.

name: plotOptions-series-events-click
title: click
description:
Fires when the series is clicked. One parameter, `event`, is passed
to the function, containing common event information. Additionally,
`event.point` holds a pointer to the nearest point on the graph.

name: plotOptions-series-events-hide
title: hide
description:
Fires when the series is hidden after chart generation time, either
by clicking the legend item or by calling `.hide()`.

name: plotOptions-series-events-mouseOut
title: mouseOut
description:
Fires when the mouse leaves the graph. One parameter, `event`, is
passed to the function, containing common event information. If the
[stickyTracking](#plotOptions.series) option is true, `mouseOut`
doesn't happen before the mouse enters another graph or leaves the
plot area.

name: plotOptions-series-events-mouseOver
title: mouseOver
description:
Fires when the mouse enters the graph. One parameter, `event`, is
passed to the function, containing common event information.

name: plotOptions-series-events-show
title: show
description:
Fires when the series is shown after chart generation time, either
by clicking the legend item or by calling `.show()`.

name: plotOptions-series-findNearestPointBy
title: findNearestPointBy
description:
Determines whether the series should look for the nearest point
in both dimensions or just the x-dimension when hovering the series.
Defaults to `'xy'` for scatter series and `'x'` for most other
series. If the data has duplicate x-values, it is recommended to
set this to `'xy'` to allow hovering over all points.

Applies only to series types using nearest neighbor search (not
direct hover) for tooltip.

name: plotOptions-series-inactiveOtherPoints
title: inactiveOtherPoints
description:
Highlight only the hovered point and fade the remaining points.

Scatter-type series require enabling the 'inactive' marker state and
adjusting opacity. Note that this approach could affect performance
with large datasets.

name: plotOptions-series-includeInDataExport
title: includeInDataExport
description:
When set to `false` will prevent the series data from being included in
any form of data export.

Since version 6.0.0 until 7.1.0 the option was existing undocumented
as `includeInCSVExport`.

name: plotOptions-series-joinBy
title: joinBy
description:
What property to join the `mapData` to the value data. For example,
if joinBy is "code", the mapData items with a specific code is merged
into the data with the same code. For maps loaded from GeoJSON, the
keys may be held in each point's `properties` object.

The joinBy option can also be an array of two values, where the first
points to a key in the `mapData`, and the second points to another
key in the `data`.

When joinBy is `null`, the map items are joined by their position in
the array, which performs much better in maps with many data points.
This is the recommended option if you are printing more than a
thousand data points and have a backend that can preprocess the data
into a parallel array of the mapData.

name: plotOptions-series-keys
title: keys
description:
An array specifying which option maps to which key in the data point
array. This makes it convenient to work with unstructured data arrays
from different sources.

name: plotOptions-series-legendSymbol
title: legendSymbol
description:
What type of legend symbol to render for this series. Can be one of
`areaMarker`, `lineMarker` or `rectangle`.

name: plotOptions-series-legendSymbolColor
title: legendSymbolColor
description:
Defines the color of the legend symbol for this series. Defaults to
undefined, in which case the series color is used. Does not work with
styled mode.

name: plotOptions-series-linecap
title: linecap
description: The line cap used for line ends and line joins on the graph.

name: plotOptions-series-marker
title: marker
description:
Options for the point markers of line and scatter-like series. Properties
like `fillColor`, `lineColor` and `lineWidth` define the visual
appearance of the markers. The `symbol` option defines the shape. Other
series types, like column series, don't have markers, but have visual
options on the series level instead.

In styled mode, the markers can be styled with the `.highcharts-point`,
`.highcharts-point-hover` and `.highcharts-point-select` class names.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable or disable the point marker. If `undefined`, the markers
are hidden when the data is dense, and shown for more widespread
data points.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-enabledThreshold
title: enabledThreshold
description:
The threshold for how dense the point markers should be before
they are hidden, given that `enabled` is not defined. The number
indicates the horizontal distance between the two closest points
in the series, as multiples of the `marker.radius`. In other
words, the default value of 2 means points are hidden if
overlapping horizontally.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
The fill color of the point marker. When `undefined`, the series'
or point's color is used.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-height
title: height
description:
Image markers only. Set the image width explicitly. When using
this option, a `width` must also be set.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the point marker's outline. When `undefined`, the
series' or point's color is used.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The width of the point marker's outline.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-radius
title: radius
description: The radius of the point marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states
title: states
description: States for a single point marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover
title: hover
description: The hover state for a single point marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when hovering over the marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the point marker.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
The fill color of the marker in hover state. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's fillColor for normal
state is used.

name: plotOptions-series-marker-states-hover-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the point marker's outline. When
