The rank for this point's data label in case of collision. If two
data labels are about to overlap, only the one with the highest
`labelrank` will be drawn.

name: series-dataLabels-nullFormat
title: nullFormat
description:
Format for points with the value of null. Works analogously to
[format](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.format). `nullFormat` can
be applied only to series which support displaying null points.
`heatmap` and `tilemap` supports `nullFormat` by default while the
following series requires [#series.nullInteraction] set to `true`:
`line`, `spline`, `area`, `area-spline`, `column`, `bar`, and
`timeline`. Does not work with series that don't display null
points, like `pie`.

name: series-dataLabels-nullFormatter
title: nullFormatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function that defines formatting for points
with the value of null. Works analogously to
[formatter](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.formatter).
`nullFormatter` can be applied only to series which support
displaying null points. `heatmap` and `tilemap` supports
`nullFormatter` by default while the following series requires
(series.nullInteraction)[#series.nullInteraction]
set to `true`: `line`, `spline`, `area`, `area-spline`, `column`,
`bar`, and `timeline`. Does not work with series that don't display
null points, like `pie`.

name: series-dataLabels-overflow
title: overflow
description:
How to handle data labels that flow outside the plot area. The
default is `"justify"`, which aligns them inside the plot area.
For columns and bars, this means it will be moved inside the bar.
To display data labels outside the plot area, set `crop` to
`false` and `overflow` to `"allow"`.

name: series-dataLabels-padding
title: padding
description:
When either the `borderWidth` or the `backgroundColor` is set,
this is the padding within the box.

An array of numbers sets padding for the respective sides. An array
of two numbers repeats the values for the horizontal and vertical
sides.

name: series-dataLabels-position
title: position
description:
Aligns data labels relative to points. If `center` alignment is
not possible, it defaults to `right`.

name: series-dataLabels-rotation
title: rotation
description:
Text rotation in degrees. Note that due to a more complex
structure, backgrounds, borders and padding will be lost on a
rotated data label.

name: series-dataLabels-shadow
title: shadow
description:
The shadow of the box. Works best with `borderWidth` or
`backgroundColor`. Since 2.3 the shadow can be an object
configuration containing `color`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `opacity`
and `width`.

name: series-dataLabels-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the label.
Symbols are predefined functions on the Renderer object.

name: series-dataLabels-style
title: style
description:
Styles for the label. The default `color` setting is
`"contrast"`, which is a pseudo color that Highcharts picks up
and applies the maximum contrast to the underlying point item,
for example the bar in a bar chart.

The `textOutline` is a pseudo property that applies an outline of
the given width with the given color, which by default is the
maximum contrast to the text. So a bright text color will result
in a black text outline for maximum readability on a mixed
background. In some cases, especially with grayscale text, the
text outline doesn't work well, in which cases it can be disabled
by setting it to `"none"`. When `useHTML` is true, the
`textOutline` will not be picked up. In this, case, the same
effect can be achieved through the `text-shadow` CSS property. As a
complementary or alternative to the `textOutline`, a
`dataLabels.backgroundColor` can be used. It provides a more calm
impression and ensures readable text label, at the cost of a risk of
overshadowing the underlying chart elements.

For some series types, where each point has an extent, like for
example tree maps, the data label may overflow the point. There
are two strategies for handling overflow. By default, the text
will wrap to multiple lines. The other strategy is to set
`style.textOverflow` to `ellipsis`, which will keep the text on
one line plus it will break inside long words.

name: series-dataLabels-textPath
title: textPath
description:
Options for a label text which should follow marker's shape.
Border and background are disabled for a label that follows a
path.

**Note:** Only SVG-based renderer supports this option. Setting
`useHTML` to true will disable this option.

Text path support is not bundled into `highcharts.js`, and requires the
`modules/textpath.js` file. However, it is included in the script files of
those series types that use it by default.

name: series-dataLabels-textPath-attributes
title: attributes
description: Presentation attributes for the text path.

name: series-dataLabels-textPath-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable or disable `textPath` option for link's or marker's data
labels.

name: series-dataLabels-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to
[use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the labels.

name: series-dataLabels-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
The vertical alignment of a data label. Can be one of `top`,
`middle` or `bottom`. The default value depends on the data, for
instance in a column chart, the label is above positive values
and below negative values.

name: series-dataLabels-x
title: x
description:
The x position offset of the label relative to the point in
pixels.

name: series-dataLabels-y
title: y
description:
The y position offset of the label relative to the point in
pixels.

name: series-dataLabels-zIndex
title: zIndex
description:
The z index of the data labels group. Does not apply below series
level options.

Use a `zIndex` of 6 to display it above the series,
or use a `zIndex` of 2 to display it behind the series.

name: series-dataMapping
title: dataMapping

name: series-dataTable
title: dataTable
description:
Options for a specific series-level data table or an array of data
tables. The `dataTable` option can be either a configuration object or an
instance of the `DataTable` class. If a `DataTable` instance is passed,
it will be used directly. If a configuration object or an array is
passed, a new `DataTable` instance will be created based on the provided
configuration.

name: series-dragDrop
title: dragDrop
description:
The draggable-points module allows points to be moved around or modified in
the chart. In addition to the options mentioned under the `dragDrop` API
structure, the module fires three events,
[point.dragStart](plotOptions.series.point.events.dragStart),
[point.drag](plotOptions.series.point.events.drag) and
[point.drop](plotOptions.series.point.events.drop).

name: series-dragDrop-dragHandle
title: dragHandle
description: Options for the drag handles available in column series.

name: series-dragDrop-dragHandle-className
title: className
description: The class name of the drag handles. Defaults to `highcharts-drag-handle`.

name: series-dragDrop-dragHandle-color
title: color
description: The fill color of the drag handles.

name: series-dragDrop-dragHandle-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: The line color of the drag handles.

name: series-dragDrop-dragHandle-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The line width for the drag handles.

name: series-dragDrop-dragHandle-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The z index for the drag handles.

name: series-dragDrop-dragMaxX
title: dragMaxX
description: Set the maximum X value the points can be moved to.

name: series-dragDrop-dragMaxY
title: dragMaxY
description: Set the maximum Y value the points can be moved to.

name: series-dragDrop-dragMinX
title: dragMinX
description: Set the minimum X value the points can be moved to.

name: series-dragDrop-dragMinY
title: dragMinY
description: Set the minimum Y value the points can be moved to.

name: series-dragDrop-dragPrecisionX
title: dragPrecisionX
description:
The X precision value to drag to for this series. Set to 0 to disable. By
default this is disabled, except for category axes, where the default is
`1`.

name: series-dragDrop-dragPrecisionY
title: dragPrecisionY
description:
The Y precision value to drag to for this series. Set to 0 to disable. By
default this is disabled, except for category axes, where the default is
`1`.

name: series-dragDrop-dragSensitivity
title: dragSensitivity
description:
The amount of pixels to drag the pointer before it counts as a drag
operation. This prevents drag/drop to fire when just clicking or
selecting points.

name: series-dragDrop-draggableX
title: draggableX
description: Enable dragging in the X dimension.

name: series-dragDrop-draggableY
title: draggableY
description:
Enable dragging in the Y dimension. Note that this is not supported for
TreeGrid axes (the default axis type in Gantt charts).

name: series-dragDrop-groupBy
title: groupBy
description:
Group the points by a property. Points with the same property value will
be grouped together when moving.

name: series-dragDrop-guideBox
title: guideBox
description:
Style options for the guide box. The guide box has one state by default,
the `default` state.

name: series-dragDrop-guideBox-default
title: default
description: Style options for the guide box default state.

name: series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-className
title: className
description:
CSS class name of the guide box in this state. Defaults to
`highcharts-drag-box-default`.

name: series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-color
title: color
description: Guide box fill color.

name: series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-cursor
title: cursor
description: Guide box cursor.

name: series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: Color of the border around the guide box.

name: series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Width of the line around the guide box.

name: series-dragDrop-guideBox-default-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: Guide box zIndex.

name: series-dragDrop-liveRedraw
title: liveRedraw
description:
Update points as they are dragged. If false, a guide box is drawn to
illustrate the new point size.

name: series-enableMouseTracking
title: enableMouseTracking
description:
Enable or disable the mouse tracking for a specific series. This
includes point tooltips and click events on graphs and points. For
large datasets it improves performance.

name: series-events
title: events
description:
General event handlers for the series items. These event hooks can
also be attached to the series at run time using the
`Highcharts.addEvent` function.

name: series-events-checkboxClick
title: checkboxClick
description:
Fires when the checkbox next to the series' name in the legend is
clicked. One parameter, `event`, is passed to the function. The state
of the checkbox is found by `event.checked`. The checked item is
found by `event.item`. Return `false` to prevent the default action
which is to toggle the select state of the series.

name: series-events-click
title: click
description:
Fires when the series is clicked. One parameter, `event`, is passed
to the function, containing common event information. Additionally,
`event.point` holds a pointer to the nearest point on the graph.

name: series-events-hide
title: hide
description:
Fires when the series is hidden after chart generation time, either
by clicking the legend item or by calling `.hide()`.

name: series-events-mouseOut
title: mouseOut
description:
Fires when the mouse leaves the graph. One parameter, `event`, is
passed to the function, containing common event information. If the
[stickyTracking](#plotOptions.series) option is true, `mouseOut`
doesn't happen before the mouse enters another graph or leaves the
plot area.

name: series-events-mouseOver
title: mouseOver
description:
Fires when the mouse enters the graph. One parameter, `event`, is
passed to the function, containing common event information.

name: series-events-show
title: show
description:
Fires when the series is shown after chart generation time, either
by clicking the legend item or by calling `.show()`.

name: series-findNearestPointBy
title: findNearestPointBy
description:
Determines whether the series should look for the nearest point
in both dimensions or just the x-dimension when hovering the series.
Defaults to `'xy'` for scatter series and `'x'` for most other
series. If the data has duplicate x-values, it is recommended to
set this to `'xy'` to allow hovering over all points.

Applies only to series types using nearest neighbor search (not
direct hover) for tooltip.

name: series-inactiveOtherPoints
title: inactiveOtherPoints
description:
Highlight only the hovered point and fade the remaining points.

Scatter-type series require enabling the 'inactive' marker state and
adjusting opacity. Note that this approach could affect performance
with large datasets.

name: series-includeInDataExport
title: includeInDataExport
description:
When set to `false` will prevent the series data from being included in
any form of data export.

Since version 6.0.0 until 7.1.0 the option was existing undocumented
as `includeInCSVExport`.

name: series-joinBy
title: joinBy
description:
What property to join the `mapData` to the value data. For example,
if joinBy is "code", the mapData items with a specific code is merged
into the data with the same code. For maps loaded from GeoJSON, the
keys may be held in each point's `properties` object.

The joinBy option can also be an array of two values, where the first
points to a key in the `mapData`, and the second points to another
key in the `data`.

When joinBy is `null`, the map items are joined by their position in
the array, which performs much better in maps with many data points.
This is the recommended option if you are printing more than a
thousand data points and have a backend that can preprocess the data
into a parallel array of the mapData.

name: series-keys
title: keys
description:
An array specifying which option maps to which key in the data point
array. This makes it convenient to work with unstructured data arrays
from different sources.

name: series-legendSymbol
title: legendSymbol
description:
What type of legend symbol to render for this series. Can be one of
`areaMarker`, `lineMarker` or `rectangle`.

name: series-legendSymbolColor
title: legendSymbolColor
description:
Defines the color of the legend symbol for this series. Defaults to
undefined, in which case the series color is used. Does not work with
styled mode.

name: series-linecap
title: linecap
description: The line cap used for line ends and line joins on the graph.

name: series-marker
title: marker
description:
Options for the point markers of line and scatter-like series. Properties
like `fillColor`, `lineColor` and `lineWidth` define the visual
appearance of the markers. The `symbol` option defines the shape. Other
series types, like column series, don't have markers, but have visual
options on the series level instead.

In styled mode, the markers can be styled with the `.highcharts-point`,
`.highcharts-point-hover` and `.highcharts-point-select` class names.

name: series-marker-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable or disable the point marker. If `undefined`, the markers
are hidden when the data is dense, and shown for more widespread
data points.

name: series-marker-enabledThreshold
title: enabledThreshold
description:
The threshold for how dense the point markers should be before
they are hidden, given that `enabled` is not defined. The number
indicates the horizontal distance between the two closest points
in the series, as multiples of the `marker.radius`. In other
words, the default value of 2 means points are hidden if
overlapping horizontally.

name: series-marker-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
The fill color of the point marker. When `undefined`, the series'
or point's color is used.

name: series-marker-height
title: height
description:
Image markers only. Set the image width explicitly. When using
this option, a `width` must also be set.

name: series-marker-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the point marker's outline. When `undefined`, the
series' or point's color is used.

name: series-marker-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The width of the point marker's outline.

name: series-marker-radius
title: radius
description: The radius of the point marker.

name: series-marker-states
title: states
description: States for a single point marker.

name: series-marker-states-hover
title: hover
description: The hover state for a single point marker.

name: series-marker-states-hover-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when hovering over the marker.

name: series-marker-states-hover-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the point marker.

name: series-marker-states-hover-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
The fill color of the marker in hover state. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's fillColor for normal
state is used.

name: series-marker-states-hover-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the point marker's outline. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's lineColor for normal
state is used.

name: series-marker-states-hover-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description:
The width of the point marker's outline. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's lineWidth for normal
state is used.

name: series-marker-states-hover-lineWidthPlus
title: lineWidthPlus
description: The additional line width for a hovered point.

name: series-marker-states-hover-radius
title: radius
description:
The radius of the point marker. In hover state, it
defaults to the normal state's radius + 2 as per the
[radiusPlus](#plotOptions.series.marker.states.hover.radiusPlus)
option.

name: series-marker-states-hover-radiusPlus
title: radiusPlus
description:
The number of pixels to increase the radius of the
hovered point.

name: series-marker-states-normal
title: normal
description:
The normal state of a single point marker. Currently only
used for setting animation when returning to normal state
from hover.

name: series-marker-states-normal-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when returning to normal state after hovering.

name: series-marker-states-select
title: select
description:
The appearance of the point marker when selected. In order to
allow a point to be selected, set the
`series.allowPointSelect` option to true.

name: series-marker-states-select-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable visible feedback for selection.

name: series-marker-states-select-fillColor
title: fillColor
description: The fill color of the point marker.

name: series-marker-states-select-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the point marker's outline. When
`undefined`, the series' or point's color is used.

name: series-marker-states-select-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The width of the point marker's outline.

name: series-marker-states-select-radius
title: radius
description:
The radius of the point marker. In hover state, it
defaults to the normal state's radius + 2.

name: series-marker-symbol
title: symbol
description:
A predefined shape or symbol for the marker. When undefined, the
symbol is pulled from options.symbols. Other possible values are
`'circle'`, `'square'`,`'diamond'`, `'triangle'` and
`'triangle-down'`.

Additionally, the URL to a graphic can be given on this form:
`'url(graphic.png)'`. Note that for the image to be applied to
exported charts, its URL needs to be accessible by the export
server.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols`. The callback is then
used by its method name, as shown in the demo.

name: series-marker-width
title: width
description:
Image markers only. Set the image width explicitly. When using
this option, a `height` must also be set.

name: series-negativeColor
title: negativeColor
description:
The color for the parts of the graph or points that are below the
[threshold](#plotOptions.series.threshold). Note that `zones` takes
precedence over the negative color. Using `negativeColor` is
equivalent to applying a zone with value of 0.

name: series-onPoint
title: onPoint
description:
Options for the _Series on point_ feature. Only `pie` and `sunburst` series
are supported at this moment.

name: series-onPoint-connectorOptions
title: connectorOptions
description:
Options for the connector in the _Series on point_ feature.

In styled mode, the connector can be styled with the
`.highcharts-connector-seriesonpoint` class name.

name: series-onPoint-connectorOptions-dashstyle
title: dashstyle
description: A name for the dash style to use for the connector.

name: series-onPoint-connectorOptions-stroke
title: stroke
description: Color of the connector line. By default it's the series' color.

name: series-onPoint-connectorOptions-width
title: width
description: Pixel width of the connector line.

name: series-onPoint-id
title: id
description:
The `id` of the point that we connect the series to. Only points with a given
`plotX` and `plotY` values and map points are valid.

name: series-onPoint-position
title: position
description:
Options allowing to set a position and an offset of the series in the
_Series on point_ feature.

name: series-onPoint-position-offsetX
title: offsetX
description:
Series center offset from the original x position. If defined, the connector
line is drawn connecting original position with new position.

name: series-onPoint-position-offsetY
title: offsetY
description:
Series center offset from the original y position. If defined, the connector
line is drawn from original position to a new position.

name: series-onPoint-position-x
title: x
description:
X position of the series center. By default, the series is displayed on the
point that it is connected to.

name: series-onPoint-position-y
title: y
description:
Y position of the series center. By default, the series is displayed on the
point that it is connected to.

name: series-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity of a series parts: line, fill (e.g. area) and dataLabels.

name: series-point
title: point
description: Properties for each single point.

name: series-point-events
title: events
description: Events for each single point.

name: series-point-events-click
title: click
description:
Fires when a point is clicked. One parameter, `event`, is passed
to the function, containing common event information.

If the `series.allowPointSelect` option is true, the default
action for the point's click event is to toggle the point's
select state. Returning `false` cancels this action.

name: series-point-events-drag
title: drag
description:
Callback that fires while dragging a point. The mouse event is passed in
as parameter. The original data can be accessed from `e.origin`, and the
new point values can be accessed from `e.newPoints`. If there is only a
single point being updated, it can be accessed from `e.newPoint` for
simplicity, and its ID can be accessed from `e.newPointId`. The `this`
context is the point being dragged. To stop the default drag action,
return false. See [drag and drop options](plotOptions.series.dragDrop).

name: series-point-events-dragStart
title: dragStart
description:
Callback that fires when starting to drag a point. The mouse event object
is passed in as an argument. If a drag handle is used, `e.updateProp` is
set to the data property being dragged. The `this` context is the point.
See [drag and drop options](plotOptions.series.dragDrop).

name: series-point-events-drop
title: drop
description:
Callback that fires when the point is dropped. The parameters passed are
the same as for [drag](#plotOptions.series.point.events.drag). To stop
the default drop action, return false. See
[drag and drop options](plotOptions.series.dragDrop).

name: series-point-events-mouseOut
title: mouseOut
description:
Fires when the mouse leaves the area close to the point. One
parameter, `event`, is passed to the function, containing common
event information.

name: series-point-events-mouseOver
title: mouseOver
description:
Fires when the mouse enters the area close to the point. One
parameter, `event`, is passed to the function, containing common
event information.

Returning `false` cancels the default behavior, which is to show a
tooltip for the point.

name: series-point-events-remove
title: remove
description:
Fires when the point is removed using the `.remove()` method. One
parameter, `event`, is passed to the function. Returning `false`
cancels the operation.

name: series-point-events-select
title: select
description:
Fires when the point is selected either programmatically or
following a click on the point. One parameter, `event`, is passed
to the function. Returning `false` cancels the operation.

name: series-point-events-unselect
title: unselect
description:
Fires when the point is unselected either programmatically or
following a click on the point. One parameter, `event`, is passed
to the function.
 Returning `false` cancels the operation.

name: series-point-events-update
title: update
description:
Fires when the point is updated programmatically through the
`.update()` method. One parameter, `event`, is passed to the
function. The new point options can be accessed through
`event.options`. Returning `false` cancels the operation.

name: series-selected
title: selected
description:
Whether to select the series initially. If `showCheckbox` is true,
the checkbox next to the series name in the legend will be checked
for a selected series.

name: series-shadow
title: shadow
description:
Whether to apply a drop shadow to the graph line. Since 2.3 the
shadow can be an object configuration containing `color`, `offsetX`,
`offsetY`, `opacity` and `width`.

Note that in some cases, like stacked columns or other dense layouts, the
series may cast shadows on each other. In that case, the
`chart.seriesGroupShadow` allows applying a common drop shadow to the
whole series group.

name: series-showCheckbox
title: showCheckbox
description:
If true, a checkbox is displayed next to the legend item to allow
selecting the series. The state of the checkbox is determined by
the `selected` option.

name: series-showInLegend
title: showInLegend
description:
Whether to display this particular series or series type in the
legend. Standalone series are shown in legend by default, and linked
series are not. Since v7.2.0 it is possible to show series that use
colorAxis by setting this option to `true`.

name: series-sonification
title: sonification
description: Sonification/audio chart options for a series.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks
title: contextTracks
description:
Context tracks for this series. Context tracks are tracks that are not
tied to data points.

Given as an array of instrument tracks, speech tracks, or a mix of both.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen
title: activeWhen
description:
Define a condition for when a track should be active and not.

Can either be a function callback or a configuration object.

If a function is used, it should return a `boolean` for whether
or not the track should be active. The function is called for
each audio event, and receives a parameter object with `time`,
and potentially `point` and `value` properties depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-crossingDown
title: crossingDown
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was above, and is now at or
below this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-crossingUp
title: crossingUp
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was below, and is now at or
above this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-max
title: max
description: Track is only active when `prop` is below or at this value.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-min
title: min
description: Track is only active when `prop` is above or at this value.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-activeWhen-prop
title: prop
description: The point property to compare, for example `y` or `x`.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-instrument
title: instrument
description:
Instrument to use for playing.

Can either be a string referencing a synth preset, or it can be
a synth configuration object.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-frequency
title: frequency
description: Frequency in Hertz of notes. Overrides pitch mapping if set.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-gapBetweenNotes
title: gapBetweenNotes
description:
Gap in milliseconds between notes if pitch is mapped to an
array of notes.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-highpass
title: highpass
description:
Mapping options for the highpass filter.

A highpass filter lets high frequencies through, but stops
low frequencies, making the sound thinner.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-highpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-highpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-lowpass
title: lowpass
description:
Mapping options for the lowpass filter.

A lowpass filter lets low frequencies through, but stops high
frequencies, making the sound more dull.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-lowpass-frequency
title: frequency
description: Map to filter frequency in Hertz from 1 to 20,000Hz.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-lowpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:
Map to filter resonance in dB. Can be negative to cause a
dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-noteDuration
title: noteDuration
description:
Note duration determines for how long a note plays, in
milliseconds.

It only affects instruments that are able to play
continuous sustained notes. Examples of these instruments
from the presets include `flute`, `saxophone`, `trumpet`,
`sawsynth`, `wobble`, `basic1`, `basic2`, `sine`,
`sineGlide`, `triangle`, `square`, `sawtooth`, `noise`,
`filteredNoise`, and `wind`.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-pan
title: pan
description:
Pan refers to the stereo panning position of the sound.
It is defined from -1 (left) to 1 (right).

By default it is mapped to `x`, making the sound move from
left to right as the chart plays.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-pitch
title: pitch
description:
Musical pitch refers to how high or low notes are played.

By default it is mapped to `y` so low `y` values are played
with a lower pitch, and high values are played with a higher
pitch.

Pitch mapping has a few extra features compared to other
audio parameters.

Firstly, it accepts not only number values, but also string
values denoting note names. These are given in the form
`<note><octave>`, for example `"c6"` or `"F#2"`.

Secondly, it is possible to map pitch to an array of notes.
In this case, the `[gapBetweenNotes](#sonification.defaultInstrumentOptions.mapping.gapBetweenNotes)`
mapping determines the delay between these notes.

Thirdly, it is possible to define a musical scale to follow
when mapping.

Can be set to a fixed value, an array, a prop to map to, a
function, or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-pitch-scale
title: scale
description:
Map pitches to a musical scale. The scale is defined as an
array of semitone offsets from the root note.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-playDelay
title: playDelay
description:
Milliseconds to wait before playing, comes in addition to
the time determined by the `time` mapping.

Can also be negative to play before the mapped time.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time
title: time
description:
Time mapping determines what time each point plays. It is
defined as an offset in milliseconds, where 0 means it
plays immediately when the chart is sonified.

By default time is mapped to `x`, meaning points with the
lowest `x` value plays first, and points with the highest
`x` value plays last.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:
A point property to map the mapping parameter to.

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-value
title: value
description:
A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

For example, if mapping to `y`, setting value to `4` will
map as if all points had a y value of 4.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-time-within
title: within
description:
What data values to map the parameter within.

Mapping within `"series"` will make the lowest value point
in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

Mapping within `"chart"` will make the lowest value point in
the whole chart map to the min audio parameter value, and
the highest value in the whole chart will map to the max
audio parameter.

You can also map within the X or Y axis of each series.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-tremolo
title: tremolo
description:
Mapping options for tremolo effects.

Tremolo is repeated changes of volume over time.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-tremolo-depth
title: depth
description:
Map to tremolo depth, from 0 to 1.

This determines the intensity of the tremolo effect, how
much the volume changes.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-tremolo-speed
title: speed
description:
Map to tremolo speed, from 0 to 1.

This determines the speed of the tremolo effect, how fast
the volume changes.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-volume
title: volume
description: The volume of notes, from 0 to 1.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate
title: rate
description: Rate mapping for speech tracks.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:
A point property to map the mapping parameter to.

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-value
title: value
description:
A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

For example, if mapping to `y`, setting value to `4` will
map as if all points had a y value of 4.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-rate-within
title: within
description:
What data values to map the parameter within.

Mapping within `"series"` will make the lowest value point
in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

Mapping within `"chart"` will make the lowest value point in
the whole chart map to the min audio parameter value, and
the highest value in the whole chart will map to the max
audio parameter.

You can also map within the X or Y axis of each series.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-mapping-text
title: text
description: Text mapping for speech tracks.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-midiName
title: midiName
description:
Name to use for a track when exporting to MIDI.
By default it uses the series name if the track is related to
a series.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description: Options for point grouping, specifically for instrument tracks.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-roundToMusicalNotes
title: roundToMusicalNotes
description:
Round pitch mapping to musical notes.

If `false`, will play the exact mapped note, even if it is out
of tune compared to the musical notes as defined by 440Hz
standard tuning.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-timeInterval
title: timeInterval
description:
Set a context track to play periodically every `timeInterval`
milliseconds while the sonification is playing.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-valueInterval
title: valueInterval
description:
Set a context track to play periodically every `valueInterval`
units of a data property `valueProp` while the sonification is
playing.

For example, setting `valueProp` to `x` and `valueInterval` to 5
will play the context track for every 5th X value.

The context audio events will be mapped to time according to the
prop value relative to the min/max values for that prop.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-valueMapFunction
title: valueMapFunction
description:
How to map context events to time when using the `valueInterval`
option.

name: series-sonification-contextTracks-valueProp
title: valueProp
description: The point property to play context for when using `valueInterval`.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions
title: defaultInstrumentOptions
description: Default options for all this series' instrument tracks.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen
title: activeWhen
description:
Define a condition for when a track should be active and not.

Can either be a function callback or a configuration object.

If a function is used, it should return a `boolean` for whether
or not the track should be active. The function is called for
each audio event, and receives a parameter object with `time`,
and potentially `point` and `value` properties depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-crossingDown
title: crossingDown
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was above, and is now at or
below this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-crossingUp
title: crossingUp
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was below, and is now at or
above this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-max
title: max
description: Track is only active when `prop` is below or at this value.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-min
title: min
description: Track is only active when `prop` is above or at this value.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-prop
title: prop
description: The point property to compare, for example `y` or `x`.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-instrument
title: instrument
description:
Instrument to use for playing.

Can either be a string referencing a synth preset, or it can be
a synth configuration object.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping
title: mapping
description:
Mapping options for the audio parameters.

All parameters can be either:
 - A string, referencing a point property to map to.
 - A number, setting the value of the audio parameter directly.
 - A callback function, returning the value programmatically.
 - An object defining detailed configuration of the mapping.

If a function is used, it should return the desired value for
the audio parameter. The function is called for each audio event
to be played, and receives a context object parameter with
`time`, and potentially `point` and `value` depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point, and `value` is available if the track is used for a
context track using `valueInterval`.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-frequency
title: frequency
description: Frequency in Hertz of notes. Overrides pitch mapping if set.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-gapBetweenNotes

dip, or positive to cause a bump.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-noteDuration
title: noteDuration
description:
Note duration determines for how long a note plays, in
milliseconds.

It only affects instruments that are able to play
continuous sustained notes. Examples of these instruments
from the presets include `flute`, `saxophone`, `trumpet`,
`sawsynth`, `wobble`, `basic1`, `basic2`, `sine`,
`sineGlide`, `triangle`, `square`, `sawtooth`, `noise`,
`filteredNoise`, and `wind`.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-pan
title: pan
description:
Pan refers to the stereo panning position of the sound.
It is defined from -1 (left) to 1 (right).

By default it is mapped to `x`, making the sound move from
left to right as the chart plays.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-pitch
title: pitch
description:
Musical pitch refers to how high or low notes are played.

By default it is mapped to `y` so low `y` values are played
with a lower pitch, and high values are played with a higher
pitch.

Pitch mapping has a few extra features compared to other
audio parameters.

Firstly, it accepts not only number values, but also string
values denoting note names. These are given in the form
`<note><octave>`, for example `"c6"` or `"F#2"`.

Secondly, it is possible to map pitch to an array of notes.
In this case, the `[gapBetweenNotes](#sonification.defaultInstrumentOptions.mapping.gapBetweenNotes)`
mapping determines the delay between these notes.

Thirdly, it is possible to define a musical scale to follow
when mapping.

Can be set to a fixed value, an array, a prop to map to, a
function, or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-pitch-scale
title: scale
description:
Map pitches to a musical scale. The scale is defined as an
array of semitone offsets from the root note.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-playDelay
title: playDelay
description:
Milliseconds to wait before playing, comes in addition to
the time determined by the `time` mapping.

Can also be negative to play before the mapped time.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time
title: time
description:
Time mapping determines what time each point plays. It is
defined as an offset in milliseconds, where 0 means it
plays immediately when the chart is sonified.

By default time is mapped to `x`, meaning points with the
lowest `x` value plays first, and points with the highest
`x` value plays last.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-mapFunction

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-mapTo

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-max
title: max

The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-min
title: min

The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-mapping-time-value

A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

title: within
description:

in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

name: series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

description:
Map pitches to a musical scale. The scale is defined as an
array of semitone offsets from the root note.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-playDelay
title: playDelay
description:
Milliseconds to wait before playing, comes in addition to
the time determined by the `time` mapping.

Can also be negative to play before the mapped time.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-time
title: time
description:
Time mapping determines what time each point plays. It is
defined as an offset in milliseconds, where 0 means it
plays immediately when the chart is sonified.

By default time is mapped to `x`, meaning points with the
lowest `x` value plays first, and points with the highest
`x` value plays last.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-time-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-time-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:
A point property to map the mapping parameter to.

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-time-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-time-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-time-value
title: value
description:
A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

For example, if mapping to `y`, setting value to `4` will
map as if all points had a y value of 4.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-time-within
title: within
description:
What data values to map the parameter within.

Mapping within `"series"` will make the lowest value point
in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

Mapping within `"chart"` will make the lowest value point in
the whole chart map to the min audio parameter value, and
the highest value in the whole chart will map to the max
audio parameter.

You can also map within the X or Y axis of each series.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-tremolo
title: tremolo
description:
Mapping options for tremolo effects.

Tremolo is repeated changes of volume over time.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-tremolo-depth
title: depth
description:
Map to tremolo depth, from 0 to 1.

This determines the intensity of the tremolo effect, how
much the volume changes.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-tremolo-speed
title: speed
description:
Map to tremolo speed, from 0 to 1.

This determines the speed of the tremolo effect, how fast
the volume changes.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-volume
title: volume
description: The volume of notes, from 0 to 1.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-rate
title: rate
description: Rate mapping for speech tracks.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-rate-mapFunction
title: mapFunction
description: How to perform the mapping.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-rate-mapTo
title: mapTo
description:
A point property to map the mapping parameter to.

A negative sign `-` can be placed before the property name
to make mapping inverted.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-rate-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value for the audio parameter. This is the
highest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-rate-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value for the audio parameter. This is the
lowest value the audio parameter will be mapped to.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-rate-value
title: value
description:
A fixed value to use for the prop when mapping.

For example, if mapping to `y`, setting value to `4` will
map as if all points had a y value of 4.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-rate-within
title: within
description:
What data values to map the parameter within.

Mapping within `"series"` will make the lowest value point
in the series map to the min audio parameter value, and the
highest value will map to the max audio parameter.

Mapping within `"chart"` will make the lowest value point in
the whole chart map to the min audio parameter value, and
the highest value in the whole chart will map to the max
audio parameter.

You can also map within the X or Y axis of each series.

name: series-sonification-tracks-mapping-text
title: text
description: Text mapping for speech tracks.

name: series-sonification-tracks-midiName
title: midiName
description:
Name to use for a track when exporting to MIDI.
By default it uses the series name if the track is related to
a series.

name: series-sonification-tracks-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description: Options for point grouping, specifically for instrument tracks.

name: series-sonification-tracks-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

name: series-sonification-tracks-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: series-sonification-tracks-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: series-sonification-tracks-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: series-sonification-tracks-roundToMusicalNotes
title: roundToMusicalNotes
description:
Round pitch mapping to musical notes.

If `false`, will play the exact mapped note, even if it is out
of tune compared to the musical notes as defined by 440Hz
standard tuning.

name: series-sonification-tracks-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: series-sonification-tracks-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: series-states
title: states
description:
A collection of options for different series states.

In addition to the options documented under each state, any option from
the parent series type can be set, with exception of `data` and `states`.

name: series-states-hover
title: hover
description:
Options for the hovered series. These settings override the
normal state options when a series is moused over or touched.

name: series-states-hover-borderColor
title: borderColor
description: The border color of the point in this state.

name: series-states-hover-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: The border width of the point in this state

name: series-states-hover-brightness
title: brightness
description:
The relative brightness of the point when hovered, relative
to the normal point color.

name: series-states-hover-color
title: color
description: The color of the shape in this state.

name: series-states-hover-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable separate styles for the hovered series to visualize
that the user hovers either the series itself or the legend.

name: series-states-inactive
title: inactive
description: The opposite state of a hover for series.

name: series-states-inactive-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when not hovering over the marker.

name: series-states-inactive-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the inactive state for a series

name: series-states-inactive-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity of series elements (dataLabels, line, area).

name: series-states-normal
title: normal
description:
The normal state of a series, or for point items in column, pie
and similar series. Currently only used for setting animation
when returning to normal state from hover.

name: series-states-normal-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when returning to normal state after hovering.

name: series-states-select
title: select
description:
Specific options for point in selected states, after being
selected by
[allowPointSelect](#plotOptions.series.allowPointSelect)
or programmatically.

name: series-stickyTracking
title: stickyTracking
description:
Sticky tracking of mouse events. When true, the `mouseOut` event on a
series isn't triggered until the mouse moves over another series, or
out of the plot area. When false, the `mouseOut` event on a series is
triggered when the mouse leaves the area around the series' graph or
markers. This also implies the tooltip when not shared. When
`stickyTracking` is false and `tooltip.shared` is false, the tooltip
will be hidden when moving the mouse between series. Defaults to true
for line and area type series, but to false for columns, pies etc.

**Note:** The boost module will force this option because of
technical limitations.

name: series-tooltip
title: tooltip
description:
A configuration object for the tooltip rendering of each single
series. Properties are inherited from [tooltip](#tooltip), but only
the following properties can be defined on a series level.

name: series-tooltip-clusterFormat
title: clusterFormat
description:
The HTML of the cluster point's in the tooltip. Works only with
marker-clusters module and analogously to
[pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

The cluster tooltip can be also formatted using
`tooltip.formatter` callback function and `point.isCluster` flag.

name: series-tooltip-distance
title: distance
description: Distance from point to tooltip in pixels.

name: series-tooltip-followPointer
title: followPointer
description:
Whether the tooltip should follow the mouse as it moves across
columns, pie slices and other point types with an extent.
By default it behaves this way for pie, polygon, map, sankey
and wordcloud series by override in the `plotOptions`
for those series types.

Does not apply if [split](#tooltip.split) is `true`.

For touch moves to behave the same way, [followTouchMove](#tooltip.followTouchMove) must be `true` also.

name: series-tooltip-followTouchMove
title: followTouchMove
description:
Whether the tooltip should update as the finger moves on a touch
device. If this is `true` and [chart.panning](#chart.panning) is
set,`followTouchMove` will take over one-finger touches, so the user
needs to use two fingers for zooming and panning.

Note the difference to [followPointer](#tooltip.followPointer) that
only defines the _position_ of the tooltip. If `followPointer` is
false in for example a column series, the tooltip will show above or
below the column, but as `followTouchMove` is true, the tooltip will
jump from column to column as the user swipes across the plot area.

name: series-tooltip-footerFormat
title: footerFormat
description: A string to append to the tooltip format.

name: series-tooltip-format
title: format
description:
A [format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for the whole shared tooltip. When format strings are a requirement,
it is usually more convenient to use `headerFormat`, `pointFormat`
and `footerFormat`, but the `format` option allows combining them
into one setting.

The context of the format string is the same as that of the
`tooltip.formatter` callback.

name: series-tooltip-header
title: header
description:
Options for the tooltip header when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split)
is enabled. The header is the box containing the X value in a split
tooltip.

name: series-tooltip-header-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
Background color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: series-tooltip-header-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
Border color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: series-tooltip-header-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The width of the border for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: series-tooltip-header-distance
title: distance
description:
Distance between the plot area and the header (except the
chevron) in a split tooltip, in pixels. The default value makes
the header text align with the axis labels.

name: series-tooltip-header-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the tooltip
header. Applies only when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is
enabled.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols` the same way as for
[series.marker.symbol](plotOptions.line.marker.symbol).

name: series-tooltip-header-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the tooltip header. The default is `{ fontSize:
'1em' }`, ensuring that the header text is the same size as the
axis labels.

name: series-tooltip-headerFormat
title: headerFormat
description:
The HTML of the tooltip header line. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. The `point.key` variable
contains the category name, x value or datetime string depending on
the type of axis. For datetime axes, the `point.key` date format can
be set using `tooltip.xDateFormat`.
In v12+, locale-aware date names follow the browser's casing and can
be lower-case, so use the `ucfirst` helper (for example
`{ucfirst point.key}`) if you want a capitalized header.

name: series-tooltip-nullFormat
title: nullFormat
description:
The HTML of the null point's line in the tooltip. Works analogously
to [pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

name: series-tooltip-nullFormatter
title: nullFormatter
description:
Callback function to format the text of the tooltip for
visible null points.
Works analogously to [formatter](#tooltip.formatter), including the
`ctx` callback argument added in v12.5.0.

name: series-tooltip-pointFormat
title: pointFormat
description:
The HTML of the point's line in the tooltip. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. Furthermore, `y` can be
extended by the `tooltip.valuePrefix` and `tooltip.valueSuffix`
variables. This can also be overridden for each series, which makes
it a good hook for displaying units.

In styled mode, the dot is colored by a class name rather than the
point color.

name: series-tooltip-pointFormatter
title: pointFormatter
description:
A callback function for formatting the HTML output for a single point
in the tooltip. Like the `pointFormat` string, but with more
flexibility. Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx` as the
first argument, so that arrow functions can access the same context
as regular functions using `this`.

name: series-tooltip-position
title: position
description:
Positioning options for fixed tooltip, taking effect only when
[tooltip.fixed](#tooltip.fixed) is `true`.

name: series-tooltip-position-align
title: align
description: The horizontal alignment of the fixed tooltip.

name: series-tooltip-position-relativeTo
title: relativeTo
description:
What the fixed tooltip alignment should be relative to.

The default, `pane`, means that it is aligned within the plot
area for that given series. If the tooltip is split (as default
in Stock charts), each partial tooltip is aligned within the
series' pane.

name: series-tooltip-position-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description: The vertical alignment of the fixed tooltip.

name: series-tooltip-position-x
title: x
description:
X pixel offset from the given position. Can be used to shy away
from axis lines, grid lines etc to avoid the tooltip overlapping
other elements.

name: series-tooltip-position-y
title: y
description:
Y pixel offset from the given position. Can be used to shy away
from axis lines, grid lines etc to avoid the tooltip overlapping
other elements.

name: series-tooltip-showDelay
title: showDelay
description:
The number of milliseconds to wait until the tooltip is shown when
mouse over a point. Works on initial hover.

name: series-tooltip-valueDecimals
title: valueDecimals
description:
How many decimals to show in each series' y value. This is
overridable in each series' tooltip options object. The default is to
preserve all decimals.

name: series-tooltip-valuePrefix
title: valuePrefix
description:
A string to prepend to each series' y value. Overridable in each
series' tooltip options object.

name: series-tooltip-valueSuffix
title: valueSuffix
description:
A string to append to each series' y value. Overridable in each
series' tooltip options object.

name: series-visible
title: visible
description: Set the initial visibility of the series.

name: series-zoomEnabled
title: zoomEnabled
description:
Whether to zoom non-cartesian series. If `chart.zooming` is set, the option
allows to disable zooming on an individual non-cartesian series. By default
zooming is enabled for all series.

**Note**: This option works only for non-cartesian series.

name: series-id
title: id
description:
An id for the series. This can be used after render time to get a pointer
to the series object through `chart.get()`.

name: series-index
title: index
description:
The index of the series in the chart, affecting the internal index in the
`chart.series` array, the visible Z index as well as the order in the
legend.

name: series-legendIndex
title: legendIndex
description: The sequential index of the series in the legend.

name: series-mapData
title: mapData
description:
An array of objects containing a `geometry` or `path` definition and
optionally additional properties to join in the `data` as per the `joinBy`
option. GeoJSON and TopoJSON structures can also be passed directly into
`mapData`.

name: series-name
title: name
description:
The name of the series as shown in the legend, tooltip etc. If a `dataTable`
and `dataMapping` are used, the name defaults to the id of the primary data
table column. Otherwise, it defaults to "Series {n}", where n is the index of
the series, starting at 1.

name: series-type
title: type
description:
The type of series, for example `line` or `column`. By default, the
series type is inherited from [chart.type](#chart.type), so unless the
chart is a combination of series types, there is no need to set it on the
series level.

name: series-data
title: data
description: The series data, as an array of values, tuples or objects.

name: series<contour>
title: series<contour>

name: series<contour>-data
title: data
description:
An array of data points for the series. For the `contour` series
type, points can be given in the following ways:

1.  An array of arrays with 3 or 2 values. In this case, the values
correspond to `x,y,value`. If the first value is a string, it is
applied as the name of the point, and the `x` value is inferred.
Unlike the heatmap, the contour series data points, do not have to appear
in any specific order.

 ```js
    data: [
        [0, 9, 7],
        [1, 10, 4],
        [2, 6, 3]
    ]
 ```

2.  An array of objects with named values. The following snippet shows only a
few settings, see the complete options set below. If the total number of data
points exceeds the series' [turboThreshold](#series.contour.turboThreshold),
this option is not available.

 ```js
    data: [{
        x: 1,
        y: 3,
        value: 10,
        name: "Point2"
    }, {
        x: 1,
        y: 7,
        value: 10,
        name: "Point1"
    }]
 ```

name: series<contour>-data-value
title: value
description:
The value of the point, resulting in a color controlled by options
as set in the [colorAxis](#colorAxis) configuration.

name: series<contour>-data-x
title: x
description:
The x value of the point. For datetime axes,
the X value is the timestamp in milliseconds since 1970.

name: series<contour>-data-y
title: y
description: The y value of the point.

name: series<flowmap>
title: series<flowmap>

name: series<flowmap>-data
title: data
description:
An array of data points for the series. For the `flowmap` series
type, points can be given in the following ways:

1.  An array of arrays with options as values. In this case,
    the values correspond to `from, to, weight`. Example:
    ```js
    data: [
        ['Point 1', 'Point 2', 4]
    ]
    ```

2.  An array of objects with named values. The following snippet shows only a
    few settings, see the complete options set below.

    ```js
    data: [{
        from: 'Point 1',
        to: 'Point 2',
        curveFactor: 0.4,
        weight: 5,
        growTowards: true,
        markerEnd: {
            enabled: true,
            height: 15,
            width: 8
        }
    }]
    ```

3.   For objects with named values, instead of using the `mappoint` `id`,
     you can use `[longitude, latitude]` arrays.

     ```js
     data: [{
         from: [longitude, latitude],
         to: [longitude, latitude]
     }]
     ```

name: series<flowmap>-data-curveFactor
title: curveFactor
description:
A `curveFactor` with a higher value than 0 will curve the link clockwise.
A negative value will curve the link counter clockwise.
If the value is 0 the link will be straight.

name: series<flowmap>-data-fillColor
title: fillColor
description: The fill color of an individual link.

name: series<flowmap>-data-fillOpacity
title: fillOpacity
description: The opacity of the link color fill.

name: series<flowmap>-data-from
title: from
description:
ID referencing a map point holding coordinates of the link origin or
coordinates in terms of array of `[longitude, latitude]` or object with `lon`
and `lat` properties.

name: series<flowmap>-data-growTowards
title: growTowards
description: If set to `true`, the line will grow towards its end.

name: series<flowmap>-data-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Specify the `lineWidth` of the link.

name: series<flowmap>-data-markerEnd
title: markerEnd
description:
Specifying a `markerEnd` here will create an arrow symbol
indicating the direction of flow at the destination of one individual link.
If one has been previously specified at the higher level option it will be
overridden for the current link.

name: series<flowmap>-data-markerEnd-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the `markerEnd`.

name: series<flowmap>-data-markerEnd-height
title: height
description:
Height of the `markerEnd`. Can be a number in pixels
or a percentage based on the weight of the link.

name: series<flowmap>-data-markerEnd-markerType
title: markerType
description: Change the shape of the `markerEnd`. Can be `arrow` or `mushroom`.

name: series<flowmap>-data-markerEnd-width
title: width
description:
Width of the `markerEnd`. Can be a number in pixels
or a percentage based on the weight of the link.

name: series<flowmap>-data-opacity
title: opacity
description: The opacity of an individual link.

name: series<flowmap>-data-to
title: to
description:
ID referencing a map point holding coordinates of the link origin or
coordinates in terms of array of `[longitude, latitude]` or object with `lon`
and `lat` properties.

name: series<flowmap>-data-weight
title: weight
description:
The weight of a link determines its thickness compared to
other links.

name: series<geoheatmap>
title: series<geoheatmap>

name: series<geoheatmap>-data
title: data
description:
An array of data points for the series. For the `geoheatmap` series
type, points can be given in the following ways:

1.  An array of arrays with 3 or 2 values. In this case, the values
correspond to `lon,lat,value`. The `value` refers to the color on the `colorAxis`.

 ```js
    data: [
        [51.50, -0.12, 7],
        [54.59, -5.93, 4],
        [55.8, -4.25, 3]
    ]
 ```

2.  An array of objects with named values. The following snippet shows only a
few settings, see the complete options set below. If the total number of data
points exceeds the series' [turboThreshold](#series.heatmap.turboThreshold),
this option is not available.

 ```js
    data: [{
        lat: 51.50,
        lon: -0.12,
        value: 7,
        name: "London"
    }, {
        lat: 54.59,
        lon: -5.93,
        value: 4,
        name: "Belfast"
    }]
 ```

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-color
title: color
description:
Individual color for the point. By default the color is either used
to denote the value, or pulled from the global `colors` array.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Individual data label for each point. The options are the same as
the ones for [plotOptions.series.dataLabels](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels).

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-drilldown
title: drilldown
description:
The `id` of a series in the [drilldown.series](#drilldown.series)
array to use for a drilldown for this point.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-events
title: events
description: Individual point events

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-geometry
title: geometry
description:
For map and mapline series types, the geometry of a point.

To achieve a better separation between the structure and the data,
it is recommended to use `mapData` to define the geometry instead
of defining it on the data points themselves.

The geometry object is compatible to that of a `feature` in GeoJSON, so
features of GeoJSON can be passed directly into the `data`, optionally
after first filtering and processing it.

For pre-projected maps (like GeoJSON maps from our
[map collection](https://code.highcharts.com/mapdata/)), user has to specify
coordinates in `projectedUnits` for geometry type other than `Point`,
instead of `[longitude, latitude]`.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-geometry-coordinates
title: coordinates
description:
The geometry coordinates in terms of arrays of `[longitude, latitude]`, or
a two dimensional array of the same. The dimensionality must comply with the
`type`.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-geometry-type
title: type
description:
The geometry type. Can be one of `LineString`, `Polygon`, `MultiLineString`
or `MultiPolygon`.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-id
title: id
description:
An id for the point. This can be used after render time to get a
pointer to the point object through `chart.get()`.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-labelrank
title: labelrank
description:
When data labels are laid out on a map, Highmaps runs a simplified
algorithm to detect collision. When two labels collide, the one with
the lowest rank is hidden. By default the rank is computed from the
area.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-middleX
title: middleX
description:
The relative mid point of an area, used to place the data label.
Ranges from 0 to 1\. When `mapData` is used, middleX can be defined
there.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-middleY
title: middleY
description:
The relative mid point of an area, used to place the data label.
Ranges from 0 to 1\. When `mapData` is used, middleY can be defined
there.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-name
title: name
description:
The name of the point as shown in the legend, tooltip, dataLabel
etc.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-path
title: path
description:
For map and mapline series types, the SVG path for the shape. For
compatibility with old IE, not all SVG path definitions are supported,
but M, L and C operators are safe.

To achieve a better separation between the structure and the data,
it is recommended to use `mapData` to define that paths instead
of defining them on the data points themselves.

For providing true geographical shapes based on longitude and latitude, use
the `geometry` option instead.

name: series<geoheatmap>-data-value
title: value
description:
The value of the point, resulting in a color controlled by options
as set in the [colorAxis](#colorAxis) configuration.

name: series<heatmap>
