algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: sonification-showCrosshair
title: showCrosshair
description:
Show X and Y axis crosshairs (if they exist) as the chart plays.

Note that if multiple tracks that play at different times try to
show the crosshairs, it can be glitchy, so it is recommended in
those cases to turn this on/off for individual tracks using the
[showPlayMarker](#plotOptions.series.sonification.tracks.showPlayMarker)
option.

name: sonification-showTooltip
title: showTooltip
description:
Show tooltip as the chart plays.

Note that if multiple tracks that play at different times try to
show the tooltip, it can be glitchy, so it is recommended in
those cases to turn this on/off for individual tracks using the
[showPlayMarker](#plotOptions.series.sonification.tracks.showPlayMarker)
option.

name: sonification-updateInterval
title: updateInterval
description:
How long to wait between each recomputation of the sonification, if
the chart updates rapidly. This avoids slowing down processes like
panning. Given in milliseconds.

name: subtitle
title: subtitle
description:
The chart's subtitle. This can be used both to display a subtitle below
the main title, and to display random text anywhere in the chart. The
subtitle can be updated after chart initialization through the
`Chart.setTitle` method.

name: subtitle-align
title: align
description:
The horizontal alignment of the subtitle. Can be one of "left",
"center" and "right". Since v12, it defaults to `undefined`, meaning
the actual alignment is inherited from the alignment of the main
title.

name: subtitle-className
title: className
description:
A CSS class name to apply to the subtitle's container div,
allowing unique CSS styling for each chart.

name: subtitle-floating
title: floating
description:
When the subtitle is floating, the plot area will not move to make
space for it.

name: subtitle-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the title.

In styled mode, the subtitle style is given in the
`.highcharts-subtitle` class.

name: subtitle-text
title: text
description: The subtitle of the chart.

name: subtitle-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to
[use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the text.

name: subtitle-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
The vertical alignment of the title. Can be one of `"top"`,
`"middle"` and `"bottom"`. When middle, the subtitle behaves as
floating.

name: subtitle-x
title: x
description:
The x position of the subtitle relative to the alignment within
`chart.spacingLeft` and `chart.spacingRight`.

name: subtitle-y
title: y
description:
The y position of the subtitle relative to the alignment within
`chart.spacingTop` and `chart.spacingBottom`. By default the subtitle
is laid out below the title unless the title is floating.

name: time
title: time

name: title
title: title
description: The chart's main title.

name: title-align
title: align
description:
The horizontal alignment of the title. Can be one of "left", "center"
and "right".

Since v12 it defaults to `undefined`, meaning the alignment is
computed for best fit. If the text fits in one line, it aligned to
the center, but if it is wrapped into multiple lines, it is aligned
to the left.

name: title-className
title: className
description:
A CSS class name to apply to the title's container div,
allowing unique CSS styling for each chart.

name: title-floating
title: floating
description:
When the title is floating, the plot area will not move to make space
for it.

name: title-margin
title: margin
description:
The margin between the title and the plot area, or if a subtitle
is present, the margin between the subtitle and the plot area.

name: title-minScale
title: minScale
description:
When the title is too wide to fit in the chart, the default behavior
is to scale it down to fit, or apply word wrap if it is scaled down
to `minScale` and still doesn't fit.

The default value reflects the scale, when using default font sizes,
when the title font size matches that of the subtitle. The title
still stands out as it is bold by default.

Set `minScale` to 1 to avoid downscaling.

name: title-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the title. Use this for font styling, but use `align`,
`x` and `y` for text alignment.

Note that the default [title.minScale](#title.minScale) option also
affects the rendered font size. In order to keep the font size fixed
regardless of title length, set `minScale` to 1.

In styled mode, the title style is given in the `.highcharts-title`
class.

name: title-text
title: text
description:
The title of the chart. To disable the title, set the `text` to
`undefined`.

name: title-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to
[use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the text.

name: title-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
The vertical alignment of the title. Can be one of `"top"`,
`"middle"` and `"bottom"`. When a value is given, the title behaves
as if [floating](#title.floating) were `true`.

name: title-x
title: x
description:
The x position of the title relative to the alignment within
`chart.spacingLeft` and `chart.spacingRight`.

name: title-y
title: y
description:
The y position of the title relative to the alignment within
[chart.spacingTop](#chart.spacingTop) and [chart.spacingBottom](#chart.spacingBottom). By default it depends on the font size.

name: tooltip
title: tooltip
description:
Options for the tooltip that appears when the user hovers over a
series or point.

name: tooltip-animation
title: animation
description: Enable or disable animation of the tooltip.

name: tooltip-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
The background color or gradient for the tooltip.

In styled mode, the stroke width is set in the
`.highcharts-tooltip-box` class.

name: tooltip-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The color of the tooltip border. When `undefined` or `null`, the
border takes the color of the corresponding series or point.

By default, in light mode the border color matches the background
color because the shadow makes the tooltip stand out. In dark mode, a
visible line is used because the default shadow is too dark to be
visible on a dark background.

name: tooltip-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description: The radius of the rounded border corners.

name: tooltip-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The pixel width of the tooltip border. Defaults to 1, but with a
`borderColor` to match the background in light mode, and a visible
lighter border in dark mode.

In styled mode, the stroke width is set in the
`.highcharts-tooltip-box` class.

name: tooltip-className
title: className
description:
A CSS class name to apply to the tooltip, allowing unique CSS
styling for each chart.

**Note:** The class is applied to the SVG element of the tooltip
(the tooltip label group), not to a container div. This allows you
to style the tooltip using CSS applicable to SVG elements.

When [tooltip.outside](#tooltip.outside) is `true`, a separate
container div with class `highcharts-tooltip-container` is created
as the parent to the SVG tooltip element, but the `className` option
is still applied to the SVG element itself, not to the container.

name: tooltip-clusterFormat
title: clusterFormat
description:
The HTML of the cluster point's in the tooltip. Works only with
marker-clusters module and analogously to
[pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

The cluster tooltip can be also formatted using
`tooltip.formatter` callback function and `point.isCluster` flag.

name: tooltip-distance
title: distance
description: Distance from point to tooltip in pixels.

name: tooltip-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the tooltip.

name: tooltip-fixed
title: fixed
description:
Whether the tooltip should be fixed to one position in the chart, or
located next to the point or mouse. When the tooltip is fixed, the
position can be further specified with the
[tooltip.position](#tooltip.position) options set.

name: tooltip-followPointer
title: followPointer
description:
Whether the tooltip should follow the mouse as it moves across
columns, pie slices and other point types with an extent.
By default it behaves this way for pie, polygon, map, sankey
and wordcloud series by override in the `plotOptions`
for those series types.

Does not apply if [split](#tooltip.split) is `true`.

For touch moves to behave the same way, [followTouchMove](#tooltip.followTouchMove) must be `true` also.

name: tooltip-followTouchMove
title: followTouchMove
description:
Whether the tooltip should update as the finger moves on a touch
device. If this is `true` and [chart.panning](#chart.panning) is
set,`followTouchMove` will take over one-finger touches, so the user
needs to use two fingers for zooming and panning.

Note the difference to [followPointer](#tooltip.followPointer) that
only defines the _position_ of the tooltip. If `followPointer` is
false in for example a column series, the tooltip will show above or
below the column, but as `followTouchMove` is true, the tooltip will
jump from column to column as the user swipes across the plot area.

name: tooltip-footerFormat
title: footerFormat
description: A string to append to the tooltip format.

name: tooltip-format
title: format
description:
A [format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for the whole shared tooltip. When format strings are a requirement,
it is usually more convenient to use `headerFormat`, `pointFormat`
and `footerFormat`, but the `format` option allows combining them
into one setting.

The context of the format string is the same as that of the
`tooltip.formatter` callback.

name: tooltip-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback function to format the text of the tooltip from scratch. In
case of single or [shared](#tooltip.shared) tooltips, a string should
be returned. In case of [split](#tooltip.split) tooltips, it should
return an array where the first item is the header, and subsequent
items are mapped to the points. Return `false` to disable tooltip for
a specific point on series.

A subset of HTML is supported. Unless `useHTML` is true, the HTML of
the tooltip is parsed and converted to SVG, therefore this isn't a
complete HTML renderer. The following HTML tags are supported: `b`,
`br`, `em`, `i`, `span`, `strong`. Spans can be styled with a `style`
attribute, but only text-related CSS, that is shared with SVG, is
handled.

The context of the formatter (since v12) is the
[Point](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point)
instance. If the tooltip is shared or split, an array `this.points`
contains all points of the hovered x-value.

Common properties from the Point to use in the formatter include:

- **Point.percentage**:
  Stacked series and pies only. The point's percentage of the total.

- **Point.points**:
  In a shared or split tooltip, this is an array containing all the
  hovered points.

- **this.series**:
  The series object. The series name is available through
  `this.series.name`.

- **this.total**:
  The total value at this point's x value in a stacked series, or the
  sum of all slices in a pie series.

- **this.x**:
  The x value.

- **this.y**:
  The y value.

name: tooltip-header
title: header
description:
Options for the tooltip header when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split)
is enabled. The header is the box containing the X value in a split
tooltip.

name: tooltip-header-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
Background color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: tooltip-header-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
Border color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: tooltip-header-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The width of the border for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: tooltip-header-distance
title: distance
description:
Distance between the plot area and the header (except the
chevron) in a split tooltip, in pixels. The default value makes
the header text align with the axis labels.

name: tooltip-header-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the tooltip
header. Applies only when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is
enabled.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols` the same way as for
[series.marker.symbol](plotOptions.line.marker.symbol).

name: tooltip-header-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the tooltip header. The default is `{ fontSize:
'1em' }`, ensuring that the header text is the same size as the
axis labels.

name: tooltip-headerFormat
title: headerFormat
description:
The HTML of the tooltip header line. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. The `point.key` variable
contains the category name, x value or datetime string depending on
the type of axis. For datetime axes, the `point.key` date format can
be set using `tooltip.xDateFormat`.
In v12+, locale-aware date names follow the browser's casing and can
be lower-case, so use the `ucfirst` helper (for example
`{ucfirst point.key}`) if you want a capitalized header.

name: tooltip-hideDelay
title: hideDelay
description:
The number of milliseconds to wait until the tooltip is hidden when
mouse out from a point or chart.

name: tooltip-nullFormat
title: nullFormat
description:
The HTML of the null point's line in the tooltip. Works analogously
to [pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

name: tooltip-nullFormatter
title: nullFormatter
description:
Callback function to format the text of the tooltip for
visible null points.
Works analogously to [formatter](#tooltip.formatter), including the
`ctx` callback argument added in v12.5.0.

name: tooltip-outside
title: outside
description:
Whether to allow the tooltip to render outside the chart's SVG
element box. By default (`false`), the tooltip is rendered within the
chart's SVG element, which results in the tooltip being aligned
inside the chart area. For small charts, this may result in clipping
or overlapping. When `true`, a separate SVG element is created and
overlaid on the page, allowing the tooltip to be aligned inside the
page itself. Beware that with this option active, CSS classes on the
chart's target container, with classnames matching the pattern
'highcharts-*', will be set on the tooltip as well. This is done to
support theming for tooltips with this option.

Defaults to `true` if `chart.scrollablePlotArea` is activated,
otherwise `false`.

name: tooltip-padding
title: padding
description: Padding inside the tooltip, in pixels.

name: tooltip-pointFormat
title: pointFormat
description:
The HTML of the point's line in the tooltip. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. Furthermore, `y` can be
extended by the `tooltip.valuePrefix` and `tooltip.valueSuffix`
variables. This can also be overridden for each series, which makes
it a good hook for displaying units.

In styled mode, the dot is colored by a class name rather than the
point color.

name: tooltip-pointFormatter
title: pointFormatter
description:
A callback function for formatting the HTML output for a single point
in the tooltip. Like the `pointFormat` string, but with more
flexibility. Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx` as the
first argument, so that arrow functions can access the same context
as regular functions using `this`.

name: tooltip-position
title: position
description:
Positioning options for fixed tooltip, taking effect only when
[tooltip.fixed](#tooltip.fixed) is `true`.

name: tooltip-position-align
title: align
description: The horizontal alignment of the fixed tooltip.

name: tooltip-position-relativeTo
title: relativeTo
description:
What the fixed tooltip alignment should be relative to.

The default, `pane`, means that it is aligned within the plot
area for that given series. If the tooltip is split (as default
in Stock charts), each partial tooltip is aligned within the
series' pane.

name: tooltip-position-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description: The vertical alignment of the fixed tooltip.

name: tooltip-position-x
title: x
description:
X pixel offset from the given position. Can be used to shy away
from axis lines, grid lines etc to avoid the tooltip overlapping
other elements.

name: tooltip-position-y
title: y
description:
Y pixel offset from the given position. Can be used to shy away
from axis lines, grid lines etc to avoid the tooltip overlapping
other elements.

name: tooltip-positioner
title: positioner
description:
A callback function to place the tooltip in a custom position. The
callback receives four parameters: `labelWidth`, `labelHeight`,
`point`, and `ctx`, where point contains values for `plotX` and
`plotY` telling where the reference point is in the plot area, and
`ctx` is the tooltip context (so that arrow-functions can access the
same context as a normal function using `this`). Add
`chart.plotLeft` and `chart.plotTop` to get the full coordinates.
Since v12.6.0, the callback receives `ctx`.

To find the actual hovered `Point` instance, use
`this.chart.hoverPoint`. For shared or split tooltips, all the hover
points are available in `this.chart.hoverPoints`.

Since v7, when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) option is enabled,
positioner is called for each of the boxes separately, including
xAxis header. xAxis header is not a point, instead `point` argument
contains info: `{ plotX: Number, plotY: Number, isHeader: Boolean }`

Since v12.2, the [tooltip.fixed](#tooltip.fixed) option combined with
[tooltip.position](#tooltip.position) covers most of the use cases
for custom tooltip positioning.

The return should be an object containing x and y values, for example
`{ x: 100, y: 100 }`.

name: tooltip-shadow
title: shadow
description:
Whether to apply a drop shadow to the tooltip. Defaults to true,
unless the tooltip is [fixed](#tooltip.fixed).

name: tooltip-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the tooltip. Can
be one of: `"callout"`, `"circle"` or `"rect"`. When
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split)
option is enabled, shape is applied to all boxes except header, which
is controlled by
[tooltip.headerShape](#tooltip.headerShape).

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols` the same way as for
[series.marker.symbol](plotOptions.line.marker.symbol).

Defaults to `callout` for floating tooltip, `rect` for
[fixed](#tooltip.fixed) tooltip.

name: tooltip-showDelay
title: showDelay
description:
The number of milliseconds to wait until the tooltip is shown when
mouse over a point. Works on initial hover.

name: tooltip-stickOnContact
title: stickOnContact
description:
Prevents the tooltip from switching or closing, when touched or
pointed.

name: tooltip-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the tooltip. The tooltip can also be styled through
the CSS class `.highcharts-tooltip`.

Note that the default `pointerEvents` style makes the tooltip ignore
mouse events, so in order to use clickable tooltips, this value must
be set to `auto`.

name: tooltip-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Use HTML to render the contents of the tooltip instead of SVG. Using
HTML allows advanced formatting like tables and images in the
tooltip. It is also recommended for rtl languages as it works around
rtl bugs in early Firefox.

name: tooltip-valueDecimals
title: valueDecimals
description:
How many decimals to show in each series' y value. This is
overridable in each series' tooltip options object. The default is to
preserve all decimals.

name: tooltip-valuePrefix
title: valuePrefix
description:
A string to prepend to each series' y value. Overridable in each
series' tooltip options object.

name: tooltip-valueSuffix
title: valueSuffix
description:
A string to append to each series' y value. Overridable in each
series' tooltip options object.

name: xAxis
title: xAxis
description:
The X axis or category axis. Normally this is the horizontal axis,
though if the chart is inverted this is the vertical axis. In case of
multiple axes, the xAxis node is an array of configuration objects.

See the [Axis class](/class-reference/Highcharts.Axis) for programmatic
access to the axis.

name: xAxis-accessibility
title: accessibility
description: Accessibility options for an axis. Requires the accessibility module.

name: xAxis-accessibility-description
title: description
description: Description for an axis to expose to screen reader users.

name: xAxis-accessibility-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable axis accessibility features, including axis information in the
screen reader information region. If this is disabled on the xAxis, the
x values are not exposed to screen readers for the individual data points
by default.

name: xAxis-accessibility-rangeDescription
title: rangeDescription
description:
Range description for an axis. Overrides the default range description.
Set to empty to disable range description for this axis.

name: xAxis-allowDecimals
title: allowDecimals
description:
Whether to allow decimals in this axis' ticks. When counting
integers, like persons or hits on a web page, decimals should
be avoided in the labels. By default, decimals are allowed on small
scale axes.

name: xAxis-alternateGridColor
title: alternateGridColor
description:
When using an alternate grid color, a band is painted across the
plot area between every other grid line.

name: xAxis-className
title: className
description:
A class name that opens for styling the axis by CSS, especially in
Highcharts styled mode. The class name is applied to group elements
for the grid, axis elements and labels.

name: xAxis-crosshair
title: crosshair
description:
Configure a crosshair that follows either the mouse pointer or the
hovered point.

Support boolean or object definition. If `true`, a crosshair with
default settings will be displayed.

In styled mode, the crosshairs are styled in the
`.highcharts-crosshair`, `.highcharts-crosshair-thin` or
`.highcharts-xaxis-category` classes.

name: xAxis-crosshair-className
title: className
description: A class name for the crosshair, especially as a hook for styling.

name: xAxis-crosshair-color
title: color
description:
The color of the crosshair. Defaults to `#cccccc` for numeric and
datetime axes, and `rgba(204,214,235,0.25)` for category axes, where
the crosshair by default highlights the whole category.

name: xAxis-crosshair-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description:
The dash style for the crosshair. See
[plotOptions.series.dashStyle](#plotOptions.series.dashStyle)
for possible values.

name: xAxis-crosshair-showDelay
title: showDelay
description:
The number of milliseconds to wait until the crosshair is shown when
the mouse is over a point. Works on initial hover.

name: xAxis-crosshair-snap
title: snap
description:
Whether the crosshair should snap to the point or follow the pointer
independent of points.

name: xAxis-crosshair-width
title: width
description:
The pixel width of the crosshair. Defaults to 1 for numeric or
datetime axes, and for one category width for category axes.

name: xAxis-crosshair-zIndex
title: zIndex
description:
The Z index of the crosshair. Higher Z indices allow drawing the
crosshair on top of the series or behind the grid lines.

name: xAxis-crossing
title: crossing
description:
The value on a perpendicular axis where this axis should cross. This
is typically used on mathematical plots where the axes cross at 0.
When `crossing` is set, space will not be reserved at the sides of
the chart for axis labels and title, so those may be clipped. In this
case it is better to place the axes without the `crossing` option.

name: xAxis-endOnTick
title: endOnTick
description:
Whether to force the axis to end on a tick. Use this option with
the `maxPadding` option to control the axis end.

name: xAxis-events
title: events
description: Event handlers for the axis.

name: xAxis-events-afterSetExtremes
title: afterSetExtremes
description:
As opposed to the `setExtremes` event, this event fires after the
final min and max values are computed and corrected for `minRange`.

Fires when the minimum and maximum is set for the axis, either by
calling the `.setExtremes()` method or by selecting an area in the
chart. One parameter, `event`, is passed to the function, containing
common event information.

The new user set minimum and maximum values can be found by
`event.min` and `event.max`. These reflect the axis minimum and
maximum in axis values. The actual data extremes are found in
`event.dataMin` and `event.dataMax`.

name: xAxis-events-setExtremes
title: setExtremes
description:
Fires when the minimum and maximum is set for the axis, either by
calling the `.setExtremes()` method or by selecting an area in the
chart. One parameter, `event`, is passed to the function,
containing common event information.

The new user set minimum and maximum values can be found by
`event.min` and `event.max`. These reflect the axis minimum and
maximum in data values. When an axis is zoomed all the way out from
the "Reset zoom" button, `event.min` and `event.max` are null, and
the new extremes are set based on `this.dataMin` and `this.dataMax`.

name: xAxis-gridLineColor
title: gridLineColor
description:
Color of the grid lines extending the ticks across the plot area.

In styled mode, the stroke is given in the `.highcharts-grid-line`
class.

name: xAxis-gridLineDashStyle
title: gridLineDashStyle
description:
The dash or dot style of the grid lines. For possible values, see
[this demonstration](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/plotoptions/series-dashstyle-all/).

name: xAxis-gridLineWidth
title: gridLineWidth
description:
The width of the grid lines extending the ticks across the plot area.
Defaults to 1 on the Y axis and 0 on the X axis, except for 3d
charts and gauges.

In gauges, the grid lines are limited to the pane's `size` and
`innerSize`.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-grid-line` class.

name: xAxis-id
title: id
description:
An id for the axis. This can be used after render time to get
a pointer to the axis object through `chart.get()`.

name: xAxis-labels
title: labels
description:
The axis labels show the number or category for each tick.

Since v8.0.0: Labels are animated in categorized x-axis with
updating data if `tickInterval` and `step` is set to 1.

name: xAxis-labels-align
title: align
description:
What part of the string the given position is anchored to.
If `left`, the left side of the string is at the axis position.
Can be one of `"left"`, `"center"` or `"right"`. Defaults to
an intelligent guess based on which side of the chart the axis
is on and the rotation of the label.

name: xAxis-labels-allowOverlap
title: allowOverlap
description:
Whether to allow the axis labels to overlap. When false,
overlapping labels are hidden.

name: xAxis-labels-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the axis labels.

name: xAxis-labels-format
title: format
description:
A format string for the axis label. The context is available as
format string variables. For example, you can use `{text}` to
insert the default formatted text. The recommended way of adding
units for the label is using `text`, for example `{text} km`.

To add custom numeric or datetime formatting, use `{value}` with
formatting, for example `{value:.1f}` or `{value:%Y-%m-%d}`.

See
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for more examples of formatting.

The default value is not specified due to the dynamic
nature of the default implementation.

name: xAxis-labels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the label. The value
is given by `this.value`. Additional properties for `this` are
`axis`, `chart`, `isFirst`, `isLast` and `text` which holds the
value of the default formatter. Since v12.6.0, the callback also
receives `ctx` as the first argument, so that arrow functions can
access the same context as regular functions using `this`.

Defaults to a built in function returning a formatted string
depending on whether the axis is `category`, `datetime`,
`numeric` or other.

name: xAxis-labels-overflow
title: overflow
description:
How to handle overflowing labels on horizontal axis. If set to
`"allow"`, it will not be aligned at all. By default it
`"justify"` labels inside the chart area. If there is room to
move it, it will be aligned to the edge, else it will be removed.

name: xAxis-labels-rotation
title: rotation
description:
Rotation of the labels in degrees. When `undefined`, the
`autoRotation` option takes precedence.

name: xAxis-labels-staggerLines
title: staggerLines
description:
Horizontal axes only. The number of lines to spread the labels
over to make room or tighter labels. 0 disables staggering.

name: xAxis-labels-step
title: step
description:
To show only every _n_'th label on the axis, set the step to _n_.
Setting the step to 2 shows every other label.

By default, when 0, the step is calculated automatically to avoid
overlap. To prevent this, set it to 1\. This usually only
happens on a category axis, and is often a sign that you have
chosen the wrong axis type.

Read more at
[Axis docs](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/axes)
=> What axis should I use?

name: xAxis-labels-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the label. Use `lineClamp` to control wrapping of
category labels. Use `textOverflow: 'none'` to prevent ellipsis
(dots).

In styled mode, the labels are styled with the
`.highcharts-axis-labels` class.

name: xAxis-labels-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to [use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the labels.

name: xAxis-labels-x
title: x
description:
The x position offset of all labels relative to the tick
positions on the axis. Overrides the `labels.distance` option.

name: xAxis-labels-y
title: y
description:
The y position offset of all labels relative to the tick
positions on the axis. Overrides the `labels.distance` option.

name: xAxis-labels-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The Z index for the axis labels.

name: xAxis-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the line marking the axis itself.

In styled mode, the line stroke is given in the
`.highcharts-axis-line` or `.highcharts-xaxis-line` class.

name: xAxis-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description:
The width of the line marking the axis itself.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-axis-line` or `.highcharts-xaxis-line` class.

name: xAxis-margin
title: margin
description:
If there are multiple axes on the same side of the chart, the pixel
margin between the axes. Defaults to 0 on vertical axes, 15 on
horizontal axes.

name: xAxis-max
title: max
description:
The maximum value of the axis. If `undefined`, the max value is
automatically calculated.

If a datetime string is passed, it is parsed into epoch time
according to the time zone given in [time.timezone](#time.timezone).

If the [endOnTick](#yAxis.endOnTick) option is true, the `max` value
might be rounded up.

If a [tickAmount](#yAxis.tickAmount) is set, the axis may be extended
beyond the set max in order to reach the given number of ticks. The
same may happen in a chart with multiple axes, determined by [chart.
alignTicks](#chart), where a `tickAmount` is applied internally.

name: xAxis-maxPadding
title: maxPadding
description:
Padding of the max value relative to the length of the axis. A
padding of 0.05 will make a 100px axis 5px longer. This is useful
when you don't want the highest data value to appear on the edge
of the plot area. When the axis' `max` option is set or a max extreme
is set using `axis.setExtremes()`, the maxPadding will be ignored.

name: xAxis-min
title: min
description:
The minimum value of the axis. If `undefined`, the min value is
automatically calculated.

If a datetime string is passed, it is parsed into epoch time
according to the time zone given in [time.timezone](#time.timezone).

If the [startOnTick](#yAxis.startOnTick) option is true (default),
the `min` value might be rounded down.

The automatically calculated minimum value is also affected by
[floor](#yAxis.floor), [softMin](#yAxis.softMin),
[minPadding](#yAxis.minPadding), [minRange](#yAxis.minRange)
as well as [series.threshold](#plotOptions.series.threshold)
and [series.softThreshold](#plotOptions.series.softThreshold).

name: xAxis-minRange
title: minRange
description:
The minimum range to display on this axis. The entire axis will not
be allowed to span over a smaller interval than this. For example,
for a datetime axis the main unit is milliseconds. If minRange is
set to 3600000, you can't zoom in more than to one hour.

The default minRange for the x axis is five times the smallest
interval between any of the data points.

On a logarithmic axis, the unit for the minimum range is the power.
So a minRange of 1 means that the axis can be zoomed to 10-100,
100-1000, 1000-10000 etc.

**Note**: The `minPadding`, `maxPadding`, `startOnTick` and
`endOnTick` settings also affect how the extremes of the axis
are computed.

name: xAxis-minTickInterval
title: minTickInterval
description:
The minimum tick interval allowed in axis values. For example on
zooming in on an axis with daily data, this can be used to prevent
the axis from showing hours. Defaults to the closest distance between
two points on the axis.

name: xAxis-minorGridLineColor
title: minorGridLineColor
description:
Color of the minor, secondary grid lines.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-minor-grid-line` class.

name: xAxis-minorGridLineDashStyle
title: minorGridLineDashStyle
description:
The dash or dot style of the minor grid lines. For possible values,
see [this demonstration](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/plotoptions/series-dashstyle-all/).

name: xAxis-minorGridLineWidth
title: minorGridLineWidth
description:
Width of the minor, secondary grid lines.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-grid-line` class.

name: xAxis-minorTickColor
title: minorTickColor
description: Color for the minor tick marks.

name: xAxis-minorTickInterval
title: minorTickInterval
description:
Specific tick interval in axis units for the minor ticks. On a linear
axis, if `"auto"`, the minor tick interval is calculated as a fifth
of the tickInterval. If `undefined`, minor ticks are not shown.

On logarithmic axes, the unit is the power of the value. For example,
setting the minorTickInterval to 1 puts one tick on each of 0.1, 1,
10, 100 etc. Setting the minorTickInterval to 0.1 produces 9 ticks
between 1 and 10, 10 and 100 etc.

If user settings dictate minor ticks to become too dense, they don't
make sense, and will be ignored to prevent performance problems.

name: xAxis-minorTickLength
title: minorTickLength
description: The pixel length of the minor tick marks.

name: xAxis-minorTickPosition
title: minorTickPosition
description:
The position of the minor tick marks relative to the axis line.
 Can be one of `inside` and `outside`.

name: xAxis-minorTickWidth
title: minorTickWidth
description: The pixel width of the minor tick mark.

name: xAxis-minorTicks
title: minorTicks
description:
Enable or disable minor ticks. The interval between the minor ticks
can be controlled either by the
[minorTicksPerMajor](#xAxis.minorTicksPerMajor) setting, or as an
absolute [minorTickInterval](#xAxis.minorTickInterval) value.

On a logarithmic axis, minor ticks are laid out based on a best
guess, attempting to enter an approximate number of minor ticks
between each major tick based on
[minorTicksPerMajor](#xAxis.minorTicksPerMajor).

Prior to v6.0.0, ticks were enabled in auto layout by setting
`minorTickInterval` to `"auto"`.

name: xAxis-minorTicksPerMajor
title: minorTicksPerMajor
description:
The number of minor ticks per major tick. Works for `linear`,
`logarithmic` and `datetime` axes.

For radial axes in gauges, the default value is 10.

name: xAxis-offset
title: offset
description:
The distance in pixels from the plot area to the axis line.
A positive offset moves the axis with its line, labels and ticks
away from the plot area. This is typically used when two or more
axes are displayed on the same side of the plot. With multiple
axes the offset is dynamically adjusted to avoid collision, this
can be overridden by setting offset explicitly.

For radial axes in gauges, the offset can be a percentage string, and
defaults to render the line and ticks on the inside of the pane and
plot bands (since v13). Labels are not affected by the offset in
radial axes.

name: xAxis-opposite
title: opposite
description:
Whether to display the axis on the opposite side of the normal. The
normal is on the left side for vertical axes and bottom for
horizontal, so the opposite sides will be right and top respectively.
This is typically used with dual or multiple axes.

name: xAxis-panningEnabled
title: panningEnabled
description:
Whether to pan axis. If `chart.panning` is enabled, the option
allows to disable panning on an individual axis.

name: xAxis-reversed
title: reversed
description:
Whether to reverse the axis so that the highest number is closest
to the origin. If the chart is inverted, the x axis is reversed by
default.

name: xAxis-showEmpty
title: showEmpty
description: Whether to show the axis line and title when the axis has no data.

name: xAxis-showFirstLabel
title: showFirstLabel
description: Whether to show the first tick label.

name: xAxis-startOnTick
title: startOnTick
description:
Whether to force the axis to start on a tick. Use this option with
the `minPadding` option to control the axis start.

name: xAxis-tickColor
title: tickColor
description:
Color for the main tick marks.

In styled mode, the stroke is given in the `.highcharts-tick`
class.

name: xAxis-tickInterval
title: tickInterval
description:
The interval of the tick marks in axis units. When `undefined`, the
tick interval is computed to approximately follow the
[tickPixelInterval](#xAxis.tickPixelInterval) on linear and datetime
axes. On categorized axes, a `undefined` tickInterval will default to
1, one category. Note that datetime axes are based on milliseconds,
so for example an interval of one day is expressed as
`24 * 3600 * 1000`.

On logarithmic axes, the tickInterval is based on powers, so a
tickInterval of 1 means one tick on each of 0.1, 1, 10, 100 etc. A
tickInterval of 2 means a tick of 0.1, 10, 1000 etc. A tickInterval
of 0.2 puts a tick on 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 20,
40 etc.


If the tickInterval is too dense for labels to be drawn, Highcharts
may remove ticks.

If the chart has multiple axes, the [alignTicks](#chart.alignTicks)
option may interfere with the `tickInterval` setting.

name: xAxis-tickLength
title: tickLength
description: The pixel length of the main tick marks.

name: xAxis-tickPixelInterval
title: tickPixelInterval
description:
If tickInterval is `null` this option sets the approximate pixel
interval of the tick marks. Not applicable to categorized axis.

The tick interval is also influenced by the [minTickInterval](#xAxis.minTickInterval) option, that, by default prevents ticks from
being denser than the data points.

name: xAxis-tickPosition
title: tickPosition
description:
The position of the major tick marks relative to the axis line.
Can be one of `inside` and `outside`.

name: xAxis-tickPositioner
title: tickPositioner
description:
A callback function returning array defining where the ticks are
laid out on the axis. This overrides the default behavior of
[tickPixelInterval](#xAxis.tickPixelInterval) and [tickInterval](#xAxis.tickInterval). The automatic tick positions are accessible
through `this.tickPositions` and can be modified by the callback.
Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx` as the third
argument, so that arrow functions can access the same context as
regular functions using `this`.

name: xAxis-tickPositions
title: tickPositions
description:
An array defining where the ticks are laid out on the axis. This
overrides the default behavior of [tickPixelInterval](#xAxis.tickPixelInterval) and [tickInterval](#xAxis.tickInterval).

Note: When working with date-time axes, be aware of time zone
handling. See the [documentation on time options](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/axes#datetime)
for best practices.

name: xAxis-tickWidth
title: tickWidth
description:
The pixel width of the major tick marks. Defaults to 0 on category
axes, otherwise 1.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the `.highcharts-tick`
class, but in order for the element to be generated on category axes,
the option must be explicitly set to 1.

name: xAxis-title
title: title
description: The axis title, showing next to the axis line.

name: xAxis-title-align
title: align
description:
Alignment of the title relative to the axis values. Possible
values are "low", "middle" or "high".

name: xAxis-title-margin
title: margin
description:
The pixel distance between the axis labels or line and the title.
Defaults to 0 for horizontal axes, 10 for vertical

name: xAxis-title-offset
title: offset
description:
The distance from the plot area to the axis line. A positive
offset moves the axis with its line, labels and ticks away from
the plot area. With multiple axes the offset is dynamically
adjusted to avoid collision, this can be overridden by setting
offset explicitly.

For radial axes in gauges, the offset can be a percentage string,
and defaults to render the line and ticks on the inside of the
pane and plot bands (since v13). Labels are not affected by the
offset in radial axes.

name: xAxis-title-rotation
title: rotation
description:
The rotation of the text in degrees. 0 is horizontal, 270 is
vertical reading from bottom to top. Defaults to 0 for horizontal
axes, 270 for left-side axes and 90 for right-side axes.

name: xAxis-title-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the title. If the title text is longer than the
axis length, it will wrap to multiple lines by default. This can
be customized by setting the `lineClamp` property, by setting a
specific `width` or by setting `whiteSpace: 'nowrap'`.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-axis-title` class.

name: xAxis-title-text
title: text
description:
The actual text of the axis title. It can contain basic HTML tags
like `b`, `i` and `span` with style.

name: xAxis-title-textAlign
title: textAlign
description:
Alignment of the text, can be `"left"`, `"right"` or `"center"`.
Default alignment depends on the
[title.align](xAxis.title.align):

Horizontal axes:
- for `align` = `"low"`, `textAlign` is set to `left`
- for `align` = `"middle"`, `textAlign` is set to `center`
- for `align` = `"high"`, `textAlign` is set to `right`

Vertical axes:
- for `align` = `"low"` and `opposite` = `true`, `textAlign` is
  set to `right`
- for `align` = `"low"` and `opposite` = `false`, `textAlign` is
  set to `left`
- for `align` = `"middle"`, `textAlign` is set to `center`
- for `align` = `"high"` and `opposite` = `true` `textAlign` is
  set to `left`
- for `align` = `"high"` and `opposite` = `false` `textAlign` is
  set to `right`

name: xAxis-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The Z index for the axis group.

name: xAxis-zoomEnabled
title: zoomEnabled
description:
Whether to zoom axis. If `chart.zoomType` is set, the option allows
to disable zooming on an individual axis.

name: yAxis
title: yAxis
description:
The Y axis or value axis. Normally this is the vertical axis,
though if the chart is inverted this is the horizontal axis.
In case of multiple axes, the yAxis node is an array of
configuration objects.

See [the Axis object](/class-reference/Highcharts.Axis) for programmatic
access to the axis.

name: yAxis-accessibility
title: accessibility
description: Accessibility options for an axis. Requires the accessibility module.

name: yAxis-accessibility-description
title: description
description: Description for an axis to expose to screen reader users.

name: yAxis-accessibility-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable axis accessibility features, including axis information in the
screen reader information region. If this is disabled on the xAxis, the
x values are not exposed to screen readers for the individual data points
by default.

name: yAxis-accessibility-rangeDescription
title: rangeDescription
description:
Range description for an axis. Overrides the default range description.
Set to empty to disable range description for this axis.

name: yAxis-allowDecimals
title: allowDecimals
description:
Whether to allow decimals in this axis' ticks. When counting
integers, like persons or hits on a web page, decimals should
be avoided in the labels. By default, decimals are allowed on small
scale axes.

name: yAxis-alternateGridColor
title: alternateGridColor
description:
When using an alternate grid color, a band is painted across the
plot area between every other grid line.

name: yAxis-className
title: className
description:
A class name that opens for styling the axis by CSS, especially in
Highcharts styled mode. The class name is applied to group elements
for the grid, axis elements and labels.

name: yAxis-crosshair
title: crosshair
description:
Configure a crosshair that follows either the mouse pointer or the
hovered point.

Support boolean or object definition. If `true`, a crosshair with
default settings will be displayed.

In styled mode, the crosshairs are styled in the
`.highcharts-crosshair`, `.highcharts-crosshair-thin` or
`.highcharts-xaxis-category` classes.

name: yAxis-crosshair-className
title: className
description: A class name for the crosshair, especially as a hook for styling.

name: yAxis-crosshair-color
title: color
description:
The color of the crosshair. Defaults to `#cccccc` for numeric and
datetime axes, and `rgba(204,214,235,0.25)` for category axes, where
the crosshair by default highlights the whole category.

name: yAxis-crosshair-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description:
The dash style for the crosshair. See
[plotOptions.series.dashStyle](#plotOptions.series.dashStyle)
for possible values.

name: yAxis-crosshair-showDelay
title: showDelay
description:
The number of milliseconds to wait until the crosshair is shown when
the mouse is over a point. Works on initial hover.

name: yAxis-crosshair-snap
title: snap
description:
Whether the crosshair should snap to the point or follow the pointer
independent of points.

name: yAxis-crosshair-width
title: width
description:
The pixel width of the crosshair. Defaults to 1 for numeric or
datetime axes, and for one category width for category axes.

name: yAxis-crosshair-zIndex
title: zIndex
description:
The Z index of the crosshair. Higher Z indices allow drawing the
crosshair on top of the series or behind the grid lines.

name: yAxis-crossing
title: crossing
description:
The value on a perpendicular axis where this axis should cross. This
is typically used on mathematical plots where the axes cross at 0.
When `crossing` is set, space will not be reserved at the sides of
the chart for axis labels and title, so those may be clipped. In this
case it is better to place the axes without the `crossing` option.

name: yAxis-endOnTick
title: endOnTick
description:
Whether to force the axis to end on a tick. Use this option with
the `maxPadding` option to control the axis end.

This option is always disabled, when panning type is
either `y` or `xy`.

name: yAxis-events
title: events
description: Event handlers for the axis.

name: yAxis-events-afterSetExtremes
title: afterSetExtremes
description:
As opposed to the `setExtremes` event, this event fires after the
final min and max values are computed and corrected for `minRange`.

Fires when the minimum and maximum is set for the axis, either by
calling the `.setExtremes()` method or by selecting an area in the
chart. One parameter, `event`, is passed to the function, containing
common event information.

The new user set minimum and maximum values can be found by
`event.min` and `event.max`. These reflect the axis minimum and
maximum in axis values. The actual data extremes are found in
`event.dataMin` and `event.dataMax`.

name: yAxis-events-setExtremes
title: setExtremes
description:
Fires when the minimum and maximum is set for the axis, either by
calling the `.setExtremes()` method or by selecting an area in the
chart. One parameter, `event`, is passed to the function,
containing common event information.

The new user set minimum and maximum values can be found by
`event.min` and `event.max`. These reflect the axis minimum and
maximum in data values. When an axis is zoomed all the way out from
the "Reset zoom" button, `event.min` and `event.max` are null, and
the new extremes are set based on `this.dataMin` and `this.dataMax`.

name: yAxis-gridLineColor
title: gridLineColor
description:
Color of the grid lines extending the ticks across the plot area.

In styled mode, the stroke is given in the `.highcharts-grid-line`
class.

name: yAxis-gridLineDashStyle
title: gridLineDashStyle
description:
The dash or dot style of the grid lines. For possible values, see
[this demonstration](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/plotoptions/series-dashstyle-all/).

name: yAxis-id
title: id
description:
An id for the axis. This can be used after render time to get
a pointer to the axis object through `chart.get()`.

name: yAxis-labels-align
title: align
description:
What part of the string the given position is anchored to. Can
be one of `"left"`, `"center"` or `"right"`. The exact position
also depends on the `labels.x` setting.

Angular gauges and solid gauges defaults to `"center"`.
Solid gauges with two labels have additional option `"auto"`
for automatic horizontal and vertical alignment.

name: yAxis-labels-allowOverlap
title: allowOverlap
description:
Whether to allow the axis labels to overlap. When false,
overlapping labels are hidden.

name: yAxis-labels-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the axis labels.

name: yAxis-labels-format
title: format
description:
A format string for the axis label. The context is available as
format string variables. For example, you can use `{text}` to
insert the default formatted text. The recommended way of adding
units for the label is using `text`, for example `{text} km`.

To add custom numeric or datetime formatting, use `{value}` with
formatting, for example `{value:.1f}` or `{value:%Y-%m-%d}`.

See
[format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for more examples of formatting.

The default value is not specified due to the dynamic
nature of the default implementation.

name: yAxis-labels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the label. The value
is given by `this.value`. Additional properties for `this` are
`axis`, `chart`, `isFirst`, `isLast` and `text` which holds the
value of the default formatter. Since v12.6.0, the callback also
receives `ctx` as the first argument, so that arrow functions can
access the same context as regular functions using `this`.

Defaults to a built in function returning a formatted string
depending on whether the axis is `category`, `datetime`,
`numeric` or other.

name: yAxis-labels-overflow
title: overflow
description:
How to handle overflowing labels on horizontal axis. If set to
`"allow"`, it will not be aligned at all. By default it
`"justify"` labels inside the chart area. If there is room to
move it, it will be aligned to the edge, else it will be removed.

name: yAxis-labels-rotation
title: rotation
description:
Rotation of the labels in degrees. When `undefined`, the
`autoRotation` option takes precedence.

name: yAxis-labels-staggerLines
title: staggerLines
description:
Horizontal axes only. The number of lines to spread the labels
over to make room or tighter labels. 0 disables staggering.

name: yAxis-labels-step
title: step
description:
To show only every _n_'th label on the axis, set the step to _n_.
Setting the step to 2 shows every other label.

By default, when 0, the step is calculated automatically to avoid
overlap. To prevent this, set it to 1\. This usually only
happens on a category axis, and is often a sign that you have
chosen the wrong axis type.

Read more at
[Axis docs](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/axes)
=> What axis should I use?

name: yAxis-labels-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the label. Use `lineClamp` to control wrapping of
category labels. Use `textOverflow: 'none'` to prevent ellipsis
(dots).

In styled mode, the labels are styled with the
`.highcharts-axis-labels` class.

name: yAxis-labels-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to [use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the labels.

name: yAxis-labels-x
title: x
description:
The x position offset of all labels relative to the tick
positions on the axis. Defaults to -15 for left axis, 15 for
right axis.

name: yAxis-labels-y
title: y
description:
The y position offset of all labels relative to the tick
positions on the axis. For polar and radial axis consider the use
of the [distance](#yAxis.labels.distance) option.

name: yAxis-labels-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The Z index for the axis labels.

name: yAxis-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the line marking the axis itself.

In styled mode, the line stroke is given in the
`.highcharts-axis-line` or `.highcharts-xaxis-line` class.

name: yAxis-margin
title: margin
description:
If there are multiple axes on the same side of the chart, the pixel
margin between the axes. Defaults to 0 on vertical axes, 15 on
horizontal axes.

name: yAxis-minRange
title: minRange
description:
The minimum range to display on this axis. The entire axis will not
be allowed to span over a smaller interval than this. For example,
for a datetime axis the main unit is milliseconds. If minRange is
set to 3600000, you can't zoom in more than to one hour.

The default minRange for the x axis is five times the smallest
interval between any of the data points.

On a logarithmic axis, the unit for the minimum range is the power.
So a minRange of 1 means that the axis can be zoomed to 10-100,
100-1000, 1000-10000 etc.

**Note**: The `minPadding`, `maxPadding`, `startOnTick` and
`endOnTick` settings also affect how the extremes of the axis
are computed.

name: yAxis-minTickInterval
title: minTickInterval
description:
The minimum tick interval allowed in axis values. For example on
zooming in on an axis with daily data, this can be used to prevent
the axis from showing hours. Defaults to the closest distance between
two points on the axis.

name: yAxis-minorGridLineColor
title: minorGridLineColor
description:
Color of the minor, secondary grid lines.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-minor-grid-line` class.

name: yAxis-minorGridLineDashStyle
title: minorGridLineDashStyle
description:
The dash or dot style of the minor grid lines. For possible values,
see [this demonstration](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/plotoptions/series-dashstyle-all/).

name: yAxis-minorGridLineWidth
title: minorGridLineWidth
description:
Width of the minor, secondary grid lines.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-grid-line` class.

name: yAxis-minorTickColor
title: minorTickColor
description: Color for the minor tick marks.

name: yAxis-minorTickInterval
title: minorTickInterval
description:
Specific tick interval in axis units for the minor ticks. On a linear
axis, if `"auto"`, the minor tick interval is calculated as a fifth
of the tickInterval. If `undefined`, minor ticks are not shown.

On logarithmic axes, the unit is the power of the value. For example,
setting the minorTickInterval to 1 puts one tick on each of 0.1, 1,
10, 100 etc. Setting the minorTickInterval to 0.1 produces 9 ticks
between 1 and 10, 10 and 100 etc.

If user settings dictate minor ticks to become too dense, they don't
make sense, and will be ignored to prevent performance problems.

name: yAxis-minorTickLength
title: minorTickLength
description: The pixel length of the minor tick marks.

name: yAxis-minorTickPosition
title: minorTickPosition
description:
The position of the minor tick marks relative to the axis line.
 Can be one of `inside` and `outside`.

name: yAxis-minorTickWidth
title: minorTickWidth
description: The pixel width of the minor tick mark.

name: yAxis-minorTicks
title: minorTicks
description:
Enable or disable minor ticks. The interval between the minor ticks
can be controlled either by the
[minorTicksPerMajor](#xAxis.minorTicksPerMajor) setting, or as an
absolute [minorTickInterval](#xAxis.minorTickInterval) value.

On a logarithmic axis, minor ticks are laid out based on a best
guess, attempting to enter an approximate number of minor ticks
between each major tick based on
[minorTicksPerMajor](#xAxis.minorTicksPerMajor).

Prior to v6.0.0, ticks were enabled in auto layout by setting
`minorTickInterval` to `"auto"`.

name: yAxis-minorTicksPerMajor
title: minorTicksPerMajor
description:
The number of minor ticks per major tick. Works for `linear`,
`logarithmic` and `datetime` axes.

For radial axes in gauges, the default value is 10.

name: yAxis-offset
title: offset
description:
The distance in pixels from the plot area to the axis line.
A positive offset moves the axis with its line, labels and ticks
away from the plot area. This is typically used when two or more
axes are displayed on the same side of the plot. With multiple
axes the offset is dynamically adjusted to avoid collision, this
can be overridden by setting offset explicitly.

For radial axes in gauges, the offset can be a percentage string, and
defaults to render the line and ticks on the inside of the pane and
plot bands (since v13). Labels are not affected by the offset in
radial axes.

name: yAxis-panningEnabled
title: panningEnabled
description:
Whether to pan axis. If `chart.panning` is enabled, the option
allows to disable panning on an individual axis.

name: yAxis-plotBands-borderColor
title: borderColor
description: Border color for the plot band. Also requires `borderWidth` to be set.

name: yAxis-plotBands-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
Border radius for the plot band. Applies only to gauges. Can be a pixel
value or a percentage, for example `50%`.

name: yAxis-plotBands-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: Border width for the plot band. Also requires `borderColor` to be set.

name: yAxis-plotBands-className
title: className
description:
A custom class name, in addition to the default `highcharts-plot-band`,
to apply to each individual band.

name: yAxis-plotBands-color
title: color
description: The color of the plot band.

name: yAxis-plotBands-events
title: events
description:
An object defining mouse events for the plot band. Supported properties
are `click`, `mouseover`, `mouseout`, `mousemove`.

name: yAxis-plotBands-events-click
title: click
description: Click event on a plot band.

name: yAxis-plotBands-events-mousemove
title: mousemove
description: Mouse move event on a plot band.

name: yAxis-plotBands-events-mouseout
title: mouseout
description: Mouse out event on the corner of a plot band.

name: yAxis-plotBands-events-mouseover
title: mouseover
description: Mouse over event on a plot band.

name: yAxis-plotBands-from
title: from
description:
The start position of the plot band in axis units.

On datetime axes, the value can be given as a timestamp or a date string.

name: yAxis-plotBands-id
title: id
description: An id used for identifying the plot band in Axis.removePlotBand.

name: yAxis-plotBands-to
title: to
description:
The end position of the plot band in axis units.

On datetime axes, the value can be given as a timestamp or a date string.

name: yAxis-plotBands-zIndex
title: zIndex
description:
The z index of the plot band within the chart, relative to other
elements. Using the same z index as another element may give
unpredictable results, as the last rendered element will be on top.
Values from 0 to 20 make sense.

name: yAxis-plotLines-className
title: className
description:
A custom class name, in addition to the default `highcharts-plot-line`,
to apply to each individual line.

name: yAxis-plotLines-color
title: color
description: The color of the line.

name: yAxis-plotLines-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description:
The dashing or dot style for the plot line. For possible values see
[this overview](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/plotoptions/series-dashstyle-all/).

name: yAxis-plotLines-events
title: events
description:
An object defining mouse events for the plot line. Supported
properties are `click`, `mouseover`, `mouseout`, `mousemove`.

name: yAxis-plotLines-events-click
title: click
description: Click event on a plot band.

name: yAxis-plotLines-events-mousemove
title: mousemove
description: Mouse move event on a plot band.

name: yAxis-plotLines-events-mouseout
title: mouseout
description: Mouse out event on the corner of a plot band.

name: yAxis-plotLines-events-mouseover
title: mouseover
description: Mouse over event on a plot band.

name: yAxis-plotLines-id
title: id
description: An id used for identifying the plot line in Axis.removePlotLine.

name: yAxis-plotLines-label
title: label
description: Text labels for the plot lines

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-align
title: align
description:
Horizontal alignment of the label. Can be one of "left", "center" or
"right".

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the label. Useful properties like
the value of plot line or the range of plot band (`from` & `to`
properties) can be found in `this.options` object. Since v12.6.0, the
callback also receives `ctx` as the first argument, so that arrow functions
can access the same context as regular functions using `this`.

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-rotation
title: rotation
description:
Rotation of the text label in degrees. Defaults to 0 for horizontal plot
lines and 90 for vertical lines.

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the text label.

In styled mode, the labels are styled by the
`.highcharts-plot-line-label` class.

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-text
title: text
description: The text itself. A subset of HTML is supported.

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-textAlign
title: textAlign
description:
The text alignment for the label. While `align` determines where the
texts anchor point is placed within the plot band, `textAlign` determines
how the text is aligned against its anchor point. Possible values are
"left", "center" and "right". Defaults to the same as the `align` option.

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to [use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the labels.

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
Vertical alignment of the label relative to the plot line. Can be
one of "top", "middle" or "bottom".

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-x
title: x
description:
Horizontal position relative the alignment. Default varies by
orientation.

name: yAxis-plotLines-label-y
title: y
description:
Vertical position of the text baseline relative to the alignment. Default
varies by orientation.

name: yAxis-plotLines-labels-clip
title: clip
description: Whether to hide labels that are outside the plot area.

name: yAxis-plotLines-value
title: value
description:
The position of the line in axis units.

On datetime axes, the value can be given as a timestamp or a date string.

name: yAxis-plotLines-width
title: width
description: The width or thickness of the plot line.

name: yAxis-plotLines-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The z index of the plot line within the chart.

name: yAxis-reversed
title: reversed
description:
Whether to reverse the axis so that the highest number is closest
to the origin.

name: yAxis-showEmpty
title: showEmpty
description: Whether to show the axis line and title when the axis has no data.

name: yAxis-showFirstLabel
title: showFirstLabel
description: Whether to show the first tick label.

name: yAxis-showLastLabel
title: showLastLabel
description: Whether to show the last tick label.

name: yAxis-tickColor
title: tickColor
description:
Color for the main tick marks.

In styled mode, the stroke is given in the `.highcharts-tick`
class.

name: yAxis-tickInterval
title: tickInterval
description:
The interval of the tick marks in axis units. When `undefined`, the
tick interval is computed to approximately follow the
[tickPixelInterval](#xAxis.tickPixelInterval) on linear and datetime
axes. On categorized axes, a `undefined` tickInterval will default to
1, one category. Note that datetime axes are based on milliseconds,
so for example an interval of one day is expressed as
`24 * 3600 * 1000`.

On logarithmic axes, the tickInterval is based on powers, so a
tickInterval of 1 means one tick on each of 0.1, 1, 10, 100 etc. A
tickInterval of 2 means a tick of 0.1, 10, 1000 etc. A tickInterval
of 0.2 puts a tick on 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 20,
40 etc.


If the tickInterval is too dense for labels to be drawn, Highcharts
may remove ticks.

If the chart has multiple axes, the [alignTicks](#chart.alignTicks)
option may interfere with the `tickInterval` setting.

name: yAxis-tickLength
title: tickLength
description: The pixel length of the main tick marks.

name: yAxis-tickPosition
title: tickPosition
description:
The position of the major tick marks relative to the axis line.
Can be one of `inside` and `outside`.

name: yAxis-tickPositioner
title: tickPositioner
description:
A callback function returning array defining where the ticks are
laid out on the axis. This overrides the default behavior of
[tickPixelInterval](#xAxis.tickPixelInterval) and [tickInterval](#xAxis.tickInterval). The automatic tick positions are accessible
through `this.tickPositions` and can be modified by the callback.
Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx` as the third
argument, so that arrow functions can access the same context as
regular functions using `this`.

name: yAxis-tickPositions
title: tickPositions
description:
An array defining where the ticks are laid out on the axis. This
overrides the default behavior of [tickPixelInterval](#xAxis.tickPixelInterval) and [tickInterval](#xAxis.tickInterval).

Note: When working with date-time axes, be aware of time zone
handling. See the [documentation on time options](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/axes#datetime)
for best practices.

name: yAxis-title-align
title: align
description:
Alignment of the title relative to the axis values. Possible
values are "low", "middle" or "high".

name: yAxis-title-margin
title: margin
description:
The pixel distance between the axis labels and the title.
Positive values are outside the axis line, negative are inside.

name: yAxis-title-offset
title: offset
description:
The distance from the plot area to the axis line. A positive
offset moves the axis with its line, labels and ticks away from
the plot area. With multiple axes the offset is dynamically
adjusted to avoid collision, this can be overridden by setting
offset explicitly.

For radial axes in gauges, the offset can be a percentage string,
and defaults to render the line and ticks on the inside of the
pane and plot bands (since v13). Labels are not affected by the
offset in radial axes.

name: yAxis-title-rotation
title: rotation
description:
The rotation of the text in degrees. 0 is horizontal, 270 is
vertical reading from bottom to top. Defaults to 0 for horizontal
axes, 270 for left-side axes and 90 for right-side axes.

name: yAxis-title-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the title. If the title text is longer than the
axis length, it will wrap to multiple lines by default. This can
be customized by setting the `lineClamp` property, by setting a
specific `width` or by setting `whiteSpace: 'nowrap'`.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-axis-title` class.

name: yAxis-title-textAlign
title: textAlign
description:
Alignment of the text, can be `"left"`, `"right"` or `"center"`.
Default alignment depends on the
[title.align](xAxis.title.align):

Horizontal axes:
- for `align` = `"low"`, `textAlign` is set to `left`
- for `align` = `"middle"`, `textAlign` is set to `center`
- for `align` = `"high"`, `textAlign` is set to `right`

Vertical axes:
- for `align` = `"low"` and `opposite` = `true`, `textAlign` is
  set to `right`
- for `align` = `"low"` and `opposite` = `false`, `textAlign` is
  set to `left`
- for `align` = `"middle"`, `textAlign` is set to `center`
- for `align` = `"high"` and `opposite` = `true` `textAlign` is
  set to `left`
- for `align` = `"high"` and `opposite` = `false` `textAlign` is
  set to `right`

name: yAxis-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The Z index for the axis group.

name: yAxis-zoomEnabled
title: zoomEnabled
description:
Whether to zoom axis. If `chart.zoomType` is set, the option allows
to disable zooming on an individual axis.
